````ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_RULES, ORDER_RULES, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, STANDING_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK, RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK } from "../src/screens/Home";

/**
 * The README's moderation runbook and the console's home screen say the same thing (3c design, section 13, Task 12).
 * When decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes, or an erasure is more than a day late, the
 * home screen shows the count with the runbook's sentence for it, and each sentence is a constant of the screen. This
 * test reads README.md from the repository's root and holds the runbook to the same two constants, word for word, so
 * that what staff are told on the screen is what the operator reads in the runbook: whoever changes one changes both.
 */
const README = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md");

/** Markdown's code mark. The README sets a log line or a setting in code marks; the console shows the same words as plain text. */
const CODE_MARK = "`";

/** A text as its reader sees it: without the code marks. Nothing else is changed, so every word and every sign must agree. */
const withoutCodeMarks = (text: string): string => text.split(CODE_MARK).join("");

/** The README's lines, as written. */
function readmeLines(): string[] {
  return readFileSync(README, "utf8").split("\n");
}

/** The lines of the README's section "Moderation": from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function moderationSection(): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf("## Moderation");
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}

/** The section's runbook as its reader sees it: every line after "The runbook:", without the code marks. */
function moderationRunbook(): string {
  const section = moderationSection();
  const start = section.indexOf("The runbook:");
  return start === -1 ? "" : withoutCodeMarks(section.slice(start + 1).join("\n"));
}

/** How often `part` stands in `text`. */
const count = (text: string, part: string): number => text.split(part).length - 1;

describe("the README's moderation runbook says what the home screen says", () => {
  const sentences: [string, string][] = [
    ["decisions not released", RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
    ["late erasures", ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
  ];

  test("the README has a section Moderation, and the section has a runbook", () => {
    expect(readmeLines()).toContain("## Moderation");
    expect(moderationSection()).toContain("The runbook:");
    expect(moderationRunbook().trim()).not.toBe("");
  });

  test("neither constant holds a code mark or a line break, so reading the README without its code marks hides no difference", () => {
    for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain(CODE_MARK);
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain("\n");
      // A whole sentence: it opens with "A count of" and ends in a full stop, as the runbook's bullet writes it.
      expect(sentence.startsWith("A count of "), name).toBe(true);
      expect(sentence.endsWith("."), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
    test(`the runbook holds the home screen's sentence for ${name}, word for word`, () => {
      expect(moderationRunbook()).toContain(sentence);
    });

    test(`the sentence for ${name} stands once in the README, in that runbook: no second copy can drift from it`, () => {
      expect(count(withoutCodeMarks(readmeLines().join("\n")), sentence)).toBe(1);
      expect(count(moderationRunbook(), sentence)).toBe(1);
    });
  }

  test("both sentences stand in one bullet of the runbook, the release's first, as the home screen orders its two lines", () => {
    const bullets = moderationRunbook()
      .split("\n")
      .filter((line) => line.includes(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK) || line.includes(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
    expect(bullets).toHaveLength(1);
    const bullet = bullets[0] ?? "";
    expect(bullet.startsWith("- ")).toBe(true);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
  });
});

/**

 * describes 3e in a paragraph that opens with ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD and a bullet for each title below, and its runbook
 * gains the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h). Every number in that text is a number of STANDING_RULES or
 * REPLY_AIM_HOURS: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused, so the README cannot
 * keep a number the constants changed. A bullet added to 3e's text joins its list here.
 */
const ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD = "Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;";
const STANDING_TITLES = [
  "Strikes.",

  "Announced suspensions and the reply.",
  "Suspensions at once.",

  "Account sanctions each working day.",
  "Answering a reply.",
  "A protective suspension.",
  "A breach that lies only in a handle",
  "A notice a person did not get by mail.",
  "A measure at once while an announced suspension waits.",
  "A mark that was wrong.",
  "Reports before an account measure.",
] as const;

/** The lines of 3e's text in Moderation, without code marks: the lead paragraph and each bullet by its bold title. */
function standingLines(): { lead: string | undefined; bullets: Map<string, string[]> } {
  const section = moderationSection().map(withoutCodeMarks);
  const bullets = new Map(STANDING_TITLES.map((title) => [title as string, section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`))]));
  return { lead: section.find((line) => line.startsWith(ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD)), bullets };
}
const standingText = (): string => {
  const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
  return [lead ?? "", ...[...bullets.values()].flat()].join("\n");
};

describe("the README's account sanctions say what the constants say (3e design, section 13, Task 7)", () => {

/**
 * The README's authorities' orders (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10) and the constants they print. 3f's text
 * is the section "Authorities' orders", Upgrading from its 3f paragraph on (Task 1), Restoring's block "Restoring with
 * the keeper's copy" (Task 6) and Before going public's owner's list. Every number in it is a number of ORDER_RULES or
 * ALERT_RULES: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused but for what names a
 * reference (an article, a research finding, a row of the design's section 2, a check P1 to P8, a list's numbering, a
 * path, a date), so the README cannot keep a number the constants changed. A setting is written as the operator sets it
 * in infra/.env, an API setting with the prefix Compose maps. A section added to 3f's text joins its list here.
 */
const FENCE = "```";

/** The lines of a "## " section of the README, from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function sectionLines(heading: string): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf(heading);
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** A section's lines from the first that begins with these words to the section's end, or to the first that begins with `until`. */
function linesFrom(lines: string[], lead: string, until?: string): string[] {
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(lead));
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start);
  const end = until === undefined ? -1 : rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(until));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** Lines without their fenced code: a command's own numbers and words are not the runbook's. */
function withoutFences(lines: string[]): string[] {
  let inside = false;
  return lines.filter((line) => {
    if (line.startsWith(FENCE)) {
      inside = !inside;
      return false;
    }
    return !inside;
  });
}

const ORDERS_HEADING = "## Authorities' orders";
const ORDERS_TITLES = [
  "The contact point.",
  "On call.",
  "A removal order, step by step",
  "Other messages and orders.",
  "When nobody can act within the hour.",
  "Notifications and hand-overs.",
  "A person asks about a missing post.",
  "An author writes about an order's notice.",
  "The daily copy.",
  "A key in someone else's hands.",
  "The yearly counts.",
] as const;
const OWNERS_LEAD = "**The owner's list (sub-project 3f).**";
const OWNERS_TITLES = [
  "The Member State.",
  "The mailbox.",
  "The people's own access to the mailbox.",
  "Registering.",
  "The push hostname and ntfy's users.",
  "The phones.",
  "The keys.",
  "The papers, and counsel.",
  "The contact address.",
  "The page for the yearly report.",
  "The keeper, and the two places files rest.",
  "Decide",
  "Counsel",
] as const;

/** 3f's text, part by part, without code marks and fenced code. */
function ordersParts(): Record<"orders" | "upgrading" | "restoring" | "owners", string> {
  const read = (lines: string[]) => withoutCodeMarks(withoutFences(lines).join("\n"));
  return {
    orders: read(sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)),
    upgrading: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f)")),
    restoring: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")),
    owners: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in")),
  };
}
const ordersText = (): string => Object.values(ordersParts()).join("\n");

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const O = ORDER_RULES;
const A = ALERT_RULES;
const ORDER_NUMBERS: { constant: string; part: keyof ReturnType<typeof ordersParts>; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "ALERT_RULES.pollSeconds", part: "orders", phrase: `reads the inbox and the junk folder every ${A.pollSeconds} seconds` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes", part: "orders", phrase: `it rings every staff phone ${O.escalateMinutes} minutes after its arrival` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction", part: "orders", phrase: `one key touch for up to ${O.itemsPerAction} posts` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays", part: "orders", phrase: `alerted daily in the last ${O.holdWarningDays} days before any release` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "orders", phrase: `the address is kept for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "upgrading", phrase: `keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.copyOverdueHours", part: "orders", phrase: `once the newest copy is more than ${O.copyOverdueHours} hours old` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes", part: "owners", phrase: `bounded only by the quiet period of ${O.quietMinutes} minutes` },
];

/** What names a reference and is no number of the runbook's, taken out before the digits are counted; only the second keeps a group, the character before the name. */
const REFERENCES: RegExp[] = [
  // A path, a file or a regulation's number: whatever holds a slash.
  /[A-Za-z0-9_.()-]*[/][A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/g,
  // A sub-project's name (3f, 3d, 1b) and a phone check (P1 to P8).
  /(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])([0-9][a-f]|P[1-8])(?=[^0-9A-Za-z]|$)/gm,
  // A list's numbering.
  /^[0-9]+[.] /gm,
  // An article of an act, with its paragraphs.
  /Art(?:icle|[.]) [0-9]+(?:[(][0-9a-z]+[)])*/g,
  // A finding of the research, with its questions; a row of the design's section 2, and the section itself.
  /(?:OL|AU) E[0-9]+[.][0-9]+(?: questions [0-9]+ to [0-9]+)?/g,
  /[(]rows? [0-9]+(?: and [0-9]+)?[)]/g,
  /section [0-9]+/g,
  // A step of a list named in a sentence.
  /steps? [0-9]+/g,
  // An instant as an example of the form, a date of the year, the hand-over's user, a hash's name, a status's code.
  /[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z/g,
  /[0-9]+ March/g,
  /uid [0-9]+/g,
  /sha256/g,
  /answers 503/g,
];

describe("the README's authorities' orders say what the constants say (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10)", () => {
  test("the README has the section Authorities' orders after Moderation, and each of its parts stands there once, in W.9's order", () => {
    const lines = readmeLines();
    expect(lines.indexOf(ORDERS_HEADING)).toBeGreaterThan(lines.indexOf("## Moderation"));
    const section = sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING).map(withoutCodeMarks);
    const at = ORDERS_TITLES.map((title) => section.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)));
    for (const title of ORDERS_TITLES) expect(section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)), title).toHaveLength(1);
    expect([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(at);
  });

  test("Before going public holds the owner's list of thirteen, each line by its title, in W.10's order", () => {
    const owners = linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in").filter((line) => /^[0-9]+[.] /.test(line));
    expect(owners.map((line) => line.slice(0, line.indexOf(" ")))).toEqual(OWNERS_TITLES.map((_, n) => `${n + 1}.`));
    for (const [n, title] of OWNERS_TITLES.entries()) expect(owners[n]!.startsWith(`${n + 1}. **${title}`), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3f's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {
    const parts = ordersParts();
    for (const row of ORDER_NUMBERS) expect(parts[row.part], `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);
  });

  test("and no other number: every run of digits in it is a constant's, outside what names a reference", () => {
    const values = new Set<string>([...Object.values(O), ...Object.values(A)].filter((value) => typeof value === "number").map(String));
    const outside = REFERENCES.reduce((text, pattern) => text.replace(pattern, (_match: string, lead: unknown) => (typeof lead === "string" ? `${lead} ` : " ")), ordersText());
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a setting is written as the operator sets it in infra/.env: an API setting with its prefix", () => {
    const withMarks = [sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel"), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")]
      .flatMap((lines) => withoutFences(lines))
      .join("\n");
    for (const name of ["NOTIFY", "REPORT_HOLD", "MODERATION_RETENTION", "HOME_STATE", "CONTACT_POINT", "PUSH_ORIGIN", "APP_ORIGIN"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(`${CODE_MARK}${name}`), name).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const name of ["API_CONTACT_POINT", "API_HOME_STATE", "API_REPORT_HOLD", "API_MODERATION_RETENTION", "APP_SITE", "COMPOSE_PROFILES", "WEB_CONTACT_POINT", "WEB_HOME_STATE"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(name) || ordersText().includes(name), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test("the hand-over's and the yearly counts' commands stand in the runbook as the operator types them", () => {
    const orders = ordersParts().orders;
    for (const words of [
      "docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests",
      "handover-list",
      "handover-record",
      "handover-destroyed",
      "staff.js tco-counts <last year>",
      "docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js address-check --handle <handle> < address",
    ]) {
      expect(orders, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(readmeLines().join("\n")).toContain("docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js tco-counts <year>");
  });

  test("3f's review: a sentence of Restoring or of the orders' runbook that sets APP_SITE recreates Caddy alone, and one that sets an API switch names the start that reads it", () => {
    // Caddy reads APP_SITE only when its container is created, and the API reads its switches only at its start: a
    // setting in infra/.env alone changes nothing. Without --no-deps Compose would start the API with Caddy.
    const sentences = [...sectionLines("## Restoring"), ...sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)].flatMap((line) => line.split(/(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z`(])/));
    const site = sentences.filter((sentence) => sentence.includes("`APP_SITE="));
    const api = sentences.filter((sentence) => /`API_[A-Z_]+=/.test(sentence));
    expect(site.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
    expect(api.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
    for (const sentence of site) expect(sentence, sentence).toContain("up -d --no-deps caddy");
    for (const sentence of api) expect(sentence, sentence).toContain("up -d api");
    // operations5: a message moved between the two folders is a second row; the runbook says not to, and what then.
    expect(ordersParts().orders).toContain("Never move a message between the inbox and the junk folder");
    expect(ordersParts().orders).toContain("close the second row on Contact point with the first row's word");
  });

  test("the lines 3f made false are gone, and the hard gate reads as W.10 words it", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join("\n");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Until sub-project 3f's off-server copy of decisions");
    expect(all).not.toContain("take the app's public hostname off the tunnel and leave the console's on");
    expect(all).not.toContain("staff.js account-facts");
    expect(all).not.toContain("account-facts <handle>");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Authorities' orders before 3f.");
    expect(all).not.toContain("in their own records until sub-project 3f");
    expect(all).not.toContain("With sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well");
    expect(all).toContain("until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's handling of sealed images have both shipped and the list below is done");
  });
});

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { AuthError } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { randomToken } from "../../src/auth/crypto";
import { DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR, confirmDeletion, finishPurge, startDeletion } from "../../src/auth/flows/deletion";
import { CODE_TTL_MS, MAX_CODE_ATTEMPTS, MIN_START_RESPONSE_MS, flowKey, startEmail } from "../../src/auth/flows/email";
import { passwordSignIn } from "../../src/auth/flows/password";
import { HOUR, MINUTE } from "../../src/auth/limits";
import { hashPassword } from "../../src/auth/passwords";
import type { Session } from "../../src/auth/sessions";
import { memoryFlowHarness, type MemoryFlowHarness } from "./flow-harness";

/** The AuthError a flow rejects with; anything else fails the test. */
async function failure(promise: Promise<unknown>): Promise<AuthError> {
  try {
    await promise;
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof AuthError) return err;
    throw err;
  }
  throw new Error("expected the flow to reject");
}

const wrong = (code: string) => String((Number(code) + 1) % 1_000_000).padStart(6, "0");

/** Starts a deletion and returns its flow id with the code from the mail to the account's address. */
async function start(h: MemoryFlowHarness, session: Session, email: string) {
  const { flowId } = await startDeletion(h.deps, session, h.ctx);
  return { flowId, code: h.mailer.lastCodeFor(email)! };
}

    expect(h.mailer.sent.map((m) => [m.to, m.template, Object.keys(m.data)])).toEqual([["ada@korbat.local", "delete_account_code", ["code"]]]);
    const expiresAt = new Date(h.now().getTime() + CODE_TTL_MS);
    expect(h.codes.map((c) => [c.email, c.purpose, c.userId, c.ipHash, c.expiresAt, c.attempts])).toEqual([["ada@korbat.local", "delete_account", ada.user.id, h.ctx.ipHash, expiresAt, 0]]);
    expect(JSON.parse((await h.kv.get(flowKey(flowId)))!)).toEqual({ userId: ada.user.id });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.user.id)!.deletedAt).toBeNull();
    expect(h.sessions.filter((s) => s.revokedAt !== null)).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.events).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("allows 3 starts an hour per account, then rate_limited with a Retry-After until the window passes", async () => {
    const h = memoryFlowHarness();

    for (let i = 0; i < DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR; i++) await startDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, h.ctx);
    const refused = await failure(startDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, h.ctx));
    expect(refused).toMatchObject({ code: "rate_limited", status: 429, retryAfterSeconds: HOUR / 1000 });
    expect(h.mailer.sent).toHaveLength(DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR);
    expect(await h.kv.get(`rl:delete-start:${ada.user.id}`)).toBe(String(DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR + 1));
    // Another account's window is its own.
    const bob = h.user("bob@korbat.local");
    await startDeletion(h.deps, bob.session, h.ctx);

    expect(h.mailer.sent.map((m) => m.to)).toEqual(["ada@korbat.local", "ada@korbat.local", "ada@korbat.local", "bob@korbat.local", "ada@korbat.local"]);

    const bob = h.user("bob@korbat.local");
    // Marked deleted and nothing else, as a take-down that stopped after the mark would leave it.
    await h.deps.repo.markDeleted(ada.user.id, h.now());
    h.advance(1000);
    await finishPurge(h.deps, ada.user.id);

    expect(h.devices.map((d) => d.userId)).toEqual([bob.user.id]);

    expect(h.passkeys).toEqual([]);

      phoneHash: null,
      totpSecretEnc: null,
      totpEnabledAt: null,
      recoveryCodesHash: [],
      termsVersion: null,
      purgedAt: h.now(),
    });
    // Nothing is recorded or sent: the event and the notice belong to the confirmation.
    expect(h.events).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.mailer.sent).toEqual([]);

    const purged = structuredClone(h.users.get(ada.user.id));
    h.advance(1000);
    await finishPurge(h.deps, ada.user.id);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.user.id)).toEqual(purged);
  });

    const bob = h.user("bob@korbat.local");
    await finishPurge(h.deps, bob.user.id);
    expect(h.sessions.map((s) => s.revokedAt)).toEqual([null]);
    expect(await h.kv.get(`sess:2:${bob.session.sessionId}`)).toBeNull();
    expect(h.devices).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(h.users.get(bob.user.id)).toMatchObject({ email: "bob@korbat.local", deletedAt: null, purgedAt: null });

describe("a deleted account is invisible to sign-in", () => {
  test("the sign-in start treats the address as unknown, in the same shape and time; password sign-in is invalid_credentials and records no failure", async () => {
    const h = memoryFlowHarness();
    const ada = h.user("ada@korbat.local");
    const password = "correct horse battery staple";
    h.users.get(ada.user.id)!.passwordHash = await hashPassword(password);
    const device = { deviceId: randomToken(), platform: "web" as const };

    // While the account lives: the start sends a sign-in code, and a wrong password is a recorded failure.
    await startEmail(h.deps, { email: "ada@korbat.local", turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx);
    expect(h.codes.map((c) => c.purpose)).toEqual(["login"]);
    expect(h.mailer.sent.map((m) => m.template)).toEqual(["sign_in_code"]);
    expect(await failure(passwordSignIn(h.deps, { email: "ada@korbat.local", password: "not it", turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx))).toMatchObject({ code: "invalid_credentials", status: 401 });
    expect(h.events.map((e) => e.type)).toEqual(["signin_failure"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.user.id)!.failedLogins).toBe(1);

    const { flowId, code } = await start(h, ada.session, "ada@korbat.local");
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId, code, handle: "ada" });
    expect(h.events.map((e) => e.type)).toEqual(["signin_failure", "account_deleted"]);

    // Past the address's cooldown: the start now answers as for an address without an account, in the same shape and time.
    h.advance(MINUTE + 1);
    const startedAt = Date.now();
    const started = await startEmail(h.deps, { email: "ada@korbat.local", turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx);
    expect(Date.now() - startedAt).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(MIN_START_RESPONSE_MS - 10);
    expect(Object.keys(started)).toEqual(["flowId"]);
    expect(h.codes.map((c) => [c.purpose, c.userId])).toEqual([["signup", null]]);
    expect(h.mailer.sent.map((m) => m.template)).toEqual(["sign_in_code", "delete_account_code", "account_deleted", "sign_up_code"]);
    // The right password no longer signs in, and the failure counter and the event log do not move: there is no account to record against.
    expect(await failure(passwordSignIn(h.deps, { email: "ada@korbat.local", password, turnstileToken: "ok", ...device }, h.ctx))).toMatchObject({ code: "invalid_credentials", status: 401 });
    expect(h.events.map((e) => e.type)).toEqual(["signin_failure", "account_deleted"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.user.id)!.failedLogins).toBe(1);
  });
});

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { Platform } from "@korbat/contracts";
import pino from "pino";
import type { AuthConfig, AuthDeps, RequestContext } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { parseVersionedKey, randomToken, sha256Hex } from "../../src/auth/crypto";
import { MemoryKv } from "../../src/auth/kv";
import { createLockout } from "../../src/auth/lockout";
import type {
  ActiveSessionRow,
  AddPasskeyOutcome,
  AuthEventType,
  AuthRepo,
  DeviceRow,
  EmailCodeRow,
  LockDownInput,
  LockDownOutcome,
  NewPasskey,
  PasskeyLimits,
  PasskeyListRow,
  PasskeyRow,
  SessionListRow,
  UserRow,
} from "../../src/auth/repo";
import { createSessions, SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MS, SESSION_IDLE_MS, type Factors, type Session } from "../../src/auth/sessions";
import { devProvider } from "../../src/auth/verify/dev";
import { MemoryMailer } from "../../src/mail/memory";

export interface RecordedEvent {
  userId: string | null;
  type: AuthEventType;
  deviceId: string | null;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export const TEST_TERMS = "draft-test";

/**
 * A session of a user, as the deletion and lockdown flows revoke it and, since Task 5, as the sign-in and re-authentication
 * flows issue, resolve and rotate it. The first three fields are all those older flows read; the rest let findActiveSession
 * answer a full row.
 */
export interface RecordedSession {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  revokedAt: Date | null;
  deviceId: string;
  handle: string;
  factors: Record<string, number>;
  passkeyId: string | null;
  reauthAt: Date;
  createdAt: Date;
  lastUsedAt: Date;
  expiresAt: Date;
  absoluteExpiresAt: Date;
}

export interface RecordedDevice {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  revokedAt: Date | null;
  /** What the passkey flows read of the row: the platform for a passkey's default name and the label for the Security list. */
  platform: Platform;
  label: string | null;
  /** The keyed hash a sign-in looks a device up by; absent on the devices h.session and h.user seed, which no lookup finds. */
  deviceHash?: string;
}

/** A passkey of a user, as the registration writes it and the lockdown and the management flows read it. */
export type RecordedPasskey = PasskeyRow;

/**
 * The auth flows without a database: users, email codes, sessions, devices and passkeys live in memory, and the
 * repository fake holds only the methods the email-change (with its undo link), badge, deletion, not-me,
 * lockdown and TOTP confirmation flows call (and the lookups the sign-in starts make), checked against the real signatures. The key-value store and the
 * mailer are the in-memory ones; the clock moves only when a test says so, so expiries and timestamps
 * compare exactly; and events are kept as the server would write them to auth_events. The integration
 * harness (test/integration/flow-harness.ts) runs flows against the real repository instead.
 */
export function memoryFlowHarness(start = 1_789_000_000_000) {
  let t = start;
  const now = () => new Date(t);
  const users = new Map<string, UserRow>();
  const codes: EmailCodeRow[] = [];
  const events: RecordedEvent[] = [];
  const sessions: RecordedSession[] = [];
  const devices: RecordedDevice[] = [];
  const passkeys: RecordedPasskey[] = [];
  /**
   * When each event was recorded, at the harness clock, kept beside the events rather than on them: the tests compare
   * the events with the exact objects the flows write, and the daily passkey bound is the only reader of the times.
   */
  const eventTimes = new WeakMap<RecordedEvent, number>();
  const recordEvent = (event: RecordedEvent) => {
    events.push(event);
    eventTimes.set(event, t);
  };
  /** The handle of each account's profile, which the deletion flow compares the typed handle with. */
  const handles = new Map<string, string>();
  /** Repository methods told to fail: "takeDown" and "lockDown" each fail as a transaction that breaks off midway, after staging its writes and before any lands. */
  const faults = new Set<"takeDown" | "lockDown">();
  /** A device as the real row reads, from what the harness keeps of it; the hash and the times are placeholders no flow reads here. */
  const deviceRow = (device: RecordedDevice): DeviceRow => ({
    id: device.id,
    userId: device.userId,
    deviceHash: device.deviceHash ?? `hash-${device.id}`,
    label: device.label,
    platform: device.platform,
    firstSeenAt: now(),
    lastSeenAt: now(),
    ipHash: null,
    revokedAt: device.revokedAt,
  });
  /** A passkey with the label of the device that added it, as the real join answers it: null once that device is gone. */
  const withDevice = (passkey: RecordedPasskey): PasskeyListRow => ({ ...passkey, createdOn: devices.find((d) => d.id === passkey.createdDeviceId)?.label ?? null });
  /**
   * The daily bound's reading, as the real statement makes it: the times of the account's latest passkey_added events within
   * the window, at most `limit` of them, and the seconds until the oldest of those leaves the window.
   */
  const recentPasskeyAdditions = (userId: string, withinMs: number, limit: number) => {
    const recent = events
      .filter((e) => e.userId === userId && e.type === "passkey_added")
      .map((e) => eventTimes.get(e)!)
      .filter((at) => at > t - withinMs)
      .sort((a, b) => b - a)
      .slice(0, limit);
    const oldest = recent.at(-1);
    return { count: recent.length, retryAfterSeconds: oldest === undefined ? 0 : Math.ceil((oldest + withinMs - t) / 1000) };
  };
  /**
   * Step 1's rows for a user, as the real repository's takeDownRows writes them: live sessions revoked (their ids
   * returned), devices, codes and passkeys gone, and the WebAuthn user handle cleared (1c design, section 7.7).
   */
  const takeDownRows = (userId: string, at: Date): string[] => {
    const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
    for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = at;
    for (let i = devices.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (devices[i]!.userId === userId) devices.splice(i, 1);
    for (let i = codes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (codes[i]!.userId === userId) codes.splice(i, 1);
    for (let i = passkeys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (passkeys[i]!.userId === userId) passkeys.splice(i, 1);
    const row = users.get(userId);
    if (row) row.webauthnUserId = null;
    return live.map((s) => s.id);
  };
  const repo = {
    async findUserById(id: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const row = users.get(id);
      return row && row.deletedAt === null ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async findUserByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      // As the real lookup: the address in any case, and never a deleted row.
      const row = [...users.values()].find((u) => u.email.toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase());
      return row && row.deletedAt === null ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async setPasswordFailures(userId: string, failedLogins: number, lockedUntil: Date | null): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) {
        row.failedLogins = failedLogins;
        row.lockedUntil = lockedUntil;
      }
    },
    async createEmailCode(input: Parameters<AuthRepo["createEmailCode"]>[0]): Promise<void> {
      codes.push({ id: randomUUID(), ...input, attempts: 0, consumedAt: null, createdAt: now() });
    },
    async findEmailCode(flowId: string): Promise<EmailCodeRow | undefined> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.flowId === flowId);
      return row ? { ...row } : undefined;
    },
    async addCodeAttempt(id: string): Promise<number> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.id === id);
      if (!row) return Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
      row.attempts += 1;
      return row.attempts;
    },
    async consumeEmailCode(id: string, at: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const row = codes.find((c) => c.id === id);
      if (!row || row.consumedAt !== null) return false;
      row.consumedAt = at;
      return true;
    },
    async changeEmail(userId: string, email: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real unique index on lower(email), deleted rows included: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      for (const other of users.values()) {
        if (other.id !== userId && other.email.toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase()) {
          throw Object.assign(new Error('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_lower_idx"'), { code: "23505" });
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row) return;
      row.email = email;
      row.emailVerifiedAt = at;
    },
    async setPasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string | null, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: setting or clearing a password also clears any lockout, and records when.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { passwordHash, passwordChangedAt: at, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null });
    },
    async enableTotp(userId: string, input: { secretEnc: string; recoveryCodesHash: string[]; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: unconditional, whatever the row held, and the last accepted step starts over.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: input.secretEnc, totpEnabledAt: input.now, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: input.recoveryCodesHash });
    },
    async disableTotp(userId: string): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] });
    },
    async lockDown(userId: string, input: LockDownInput): Promise<LockDownOutcome> {
      // One transaction, as the real one: when it fails midway nothing it would have written lands.
      if (faults.has("lockDown")) throw new Error("the lockdown transaction failed midway and was rolled back");
      const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
      for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = input.now;
      for (const device of devices) if (device.userId === userId && device.revokedAt === null) device.revokedAt = input.now;
      // As the real statement: the user's passkeys created at or after `since`, plus any of theirs the caller names.
      const passkeysRemoved: string[] = [];
      for (let i = passkeys.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const passkey = passkeys[i]!;
        if (passkey.userId !== userId) continue;
        if (passkey.createdAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime() || input.passkeyIds.includes(passkey.id)) {
          passkeysRemoved.push(passkey.id);
          passkeys.splice(i, 1);
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      // As the real read of the locked row: an account that is gone has no two-factor to clear.
      const totpCleared = row !== undefined && row.deletedAt === null && row.totpEnabledAt !== null && row.totpEnabledAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime();
      if (row) {
        // The password as setPasswordHash clears it, and two-factor as disableTotp turns it off.
        Object.assign(row, { passwordHash: null, passwordChangedAt: input.now, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null });
        if (totpCleared) Object.assign(row, { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] });
      }
      recordEvent({ userId, type: input.event.type, deviceId: input.event.deviceId, metadata: { ...input.event.metadata, passkeysRemoved, totpCleared, passwordCleared: true } });
      return { sessionIds: live.map((s) => s.id), passkeysRemoved, totpCleared };
    },
    async setPhoneHash(userId: string, phoneHash: string | null): Promise<void> {
      // As the real partial unique index on phone_hash, deleted rows included: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      if (phoneHash !== null) {
        for (const other of users.values()) {
          if (other.id !== userId && other.phoneHash === phoneHash) {
            throw Object.assign(new Error('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_phone_hash_idx"'), { code: "23505" });
          }
        }
      }
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row) row.phoneHash = phoneHash;
    },
    async appendEvent(input: Parameters<AuthRepo["appendEvent"]>[0]): Promise<void> {
      recordEvent({ userId: input.userId, type: input.type, deviceId: input.deviceId ?? null, metadata: input.metadata ?? {} });
    },
    async findDeviceById(id: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === id);
      return device ? deviceRow(device) : undefined;
    },
    async ensureWebauthnUserId(userId: string, candidate: Buffer): Promise<Buffer | undefined> {
      // As the real compare-and-set: the first candidate sticks, every later call reads it back.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt !== null) return undefined;
      row.webauthnUserId ??= candidate;
      return row.webauthnUserId;
    },
    async countPasskeys(userId: string): Promise<number> {
      return passkeys.filter((p) => p.userId === userId).length;
    },
    async listPasskeys(userId: string): Promise<PasskeyListRow[]> {
      // Newest first, as the real statement orders them.
      return passkeys
        .filter((p) => p.userId === userId)
        .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.getTime() - a.createdAt.getTime())
        .map(withDevice);
    },
    async findPasskey(id: string, userId: string): Promise<PasskeyListRow | undefined> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      return passkey ? withDevice(passkey) : undefined;
    },
    async recentPasskeyAdditions(userId: string, withinMs: number, limit: number): Promise<{ count: number; retryAfterSeconds: number }> {
      return recentPasskeyAdditions(userId, withinMs, limit);
    },
    async addPasskey(input: NewPasskey, limits: PasskeyLimits): Promise<AddPasskeyOutcome> {
      // As the real transaction: the account locked, both bounds checked again, then the row and its event, or nothing.
      const row = users.get(input.userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt !== null) return { ok: false, reason: "gone" };
      if (passkeys.filter((p) => p.userId === input.userId).length >= limits.passkeys) return { ok: false, reason: "cap" };
      const additions = recentPasskeyAdditions(input.userId, limits.windowMs, limits.additions);
      if (additions.count >= limits.additions) return { ok: false, reason: "daily", retryAfterSeconds: additions.retryAfterSeconds };
      // As the real unique index on credential_id: the driver error that the flow recognises through isUniqueViolation.
      if (passkeys.some((p) => p.credentialId === input.credentialId)) {
        throw Object.assign(new Error('duplicate key value violates unique constraint "passkeys_credential_idx"'), { code: "23505" });
      }
      const passkey: RecordedPasskey = { id: randomUUID(), lastUsedAt: null, suspectAt: null, ...input };
      passkeys.push(passkey);
      recordEvent({ userId: input.userId, type: "passkey_added", deviceId: input.createdDeviceId, metadata: { passkeyId: passkey.id } });
      return { ok: true, passkey: { ...passkey } };
    },
    async renamePasskey(id: string, userId: string, name: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      if (!passkey) return false;
      passkey.name = name;
      return true;
    },
    async deletePasskey(id: string, userId: string): Promise<{ name: string } | undefined> {
      const index = passkeys.findIndex((p) => p.id === id && p.userId === userId);
      if (index === -1) return undefined;
      const [removed] = passkeys.splice(index, 1);
      return { name: removed!.name };
    },
    async findPasskeyByCredentialId(credentialId: string): Promise<PasskeyRow | undefined> {
      // As the real lookup: any account's, and the flow refuses a deleted owner through findUserById.
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.credentialId === credentialId);
      return passkey ? { ...passkey } : undefined;
    },
    async findPasskeyByCredential(credentialId: string, userId: string): Promise<PasskeyRow | undefined> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.credentialId === credentialId && p.userId === userId);
      return passkey ? { ...passkey } : undefined;
    },
    async claimPasskeyUse(id: string, newCounter: number, backedUp: boolean, at: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real conditional update: a suspect passkey never matches, and the counter must move forward unless both are zero.
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id);
      if (!passkey || passkey.suspectAt !== null) return false;
      if (!((newCounter === 0 && passkey.counter === 0) || newCounter > passkey.counter)) return false;
      passkey.counter = newCounter;
      passkey.lastUsedAt = at;
      passkey.backedUp = backedUp;
      return true;
    },
    async suspectPasskey(id: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      const passkey = passkeys.find((p) => p.id === id);
      if (passkey && passkey.suspectAt === null) passkey.suspectAt = at;
    },
    async findDevice(userId: string, deviceHashValue: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.userId === userId && d.deviceHash === deviceHashValue && d.revokedAt === null);
      return device ? deviceRow(device) : undefined;
    },
    async createDevice(input: { userId: string; deviceHash: string; label: string; platform: string; ipHash: string | null }): Promise<DeviceRow> {
      const device: RecordedDevice = { id: randomUUID(), userId: input.userId, revokedAt: null, platform: input.platform as Platform, label: input.label, deviceHash: input.deviceHash };
      devices.push(device);
      return deviceRow(device);
    },
    async touchDevice(): Promise<void> {
      // The row's last-seen and ip are placeholders no flow reads here, so touching it changes nothing observable.
    },
    async createSession(input: {
      id: string;
      userId: string;
      deviceId: string;
      now: Date;
      expiresAt: Date;
      absoluteExpiresAt: Date;
      factors?: Record<string, number>;
      passkeyId?: string | null;
    }): Promise<void> {
      // As the real insert: the reauth time is the latest of the factors, and a fresh handle stands in for the column's default.
      const factors = input.factors ?? {};
      const times = Object.values(factors);
      sessions.push({
        id: input.id,
        userId: input.userId,
        revokedAt: null,
        deviceId: input.deviceId,
        handle: randomUUID(),
        factors,
        passkeyId: input.passkeyId ?? null,
        reauthAt: times.length > 0 ? new Date(Math.max(...times)) : input.now,
        createdAt: input.now,
        lastUsedAt: input.now,
        expiresAt: input.expiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: input.absoluteExpiresAt,
      });
    },
    async findActiveSession(id: string, at: Date): Promise<ActiveSessionRow | undefined> {
      // As the real joins: the session, its account and its device must all be live.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id && s.revokedAt === null && s.expiresAt > at && s.absoluteExpiresAt > at);
      if (!row) return undefined;
      const user = users.get(row.userId);
      if (!user || user.deletedAt !== null) return undefined;
      const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === row.deviceId && d.revokedAt === null);
      if (!device) return undefined;
      return {
        id: row.id,
        userId: row.userId,
        deviceId: row.deviceId,
        role: user.role,
        onboardedAt: user.onboardedAt,
        totpEnabledAt: user.totpEnabledAt,
        reauthAt: row.reauthAt,
        lastUsedAt: row.lastUsedAt,
        expiresAt: row.expiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: row.absoluteExpiresAt,
        handle: row.handle,
        factors: row.factors,
        passkeyId: row.passkeyId,
      };
    },
    async rotateSession(id: string, newId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real statement: the primary key changes in place for a live row, and everything else stays.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id && s.revokedAt === null);
      if (!row) return false;
      row.id = newId;
      return true;
    },
    async writeFactor(id: string, kind: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      // As the real statement: the kind's time is set or replaced and the reauth time follows it.
      const row = sessions.find((s) => s.id === id);
      if (!row) return;
      row.factors = { ...row.factors, [kind]: at.getTime() };
      row.reauthAt = at;
    },
    async claimTotpStep(userId: string, step: number): Promise<boolean> {
      // As the real conditional update: a step no later than the last accepted one is refused, so a code cannot be reused.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || (row.totpLastStep !== null && row.totpLastStep >= step)) return false;
      row.totpLastStep = step;
      return true;
    },
    async revokeAllSessions(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const live = sessions.filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null);
      for (const s of live) s.revokedAt = at;
      return live.map((s) => s.id);
    },
    async listActiveSessions(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<SessionListRow[]> {
      // As the real statement: the user's sessions that are neither revoked nor expired, most recently used first, each with its device's label.
      return sessions
        .filter((s) => s.userId === userId && s.revokedAt === null && s.expiresAt > at && s.absoluteExpiresAt > at)
        .sort((a, b) => b.lastUsedAt.getTime() - a.lastUsedAt.getTime())
        .map((s) => {
          const device = devices.find((d) => d.id === s.deviceId);
          return { id: s.id, handle: s.handle, deviceLabel: device?.label ?? null, platform: device?.platform ?? "web", createdAt: s.createdAt, lastUsedAt: s.lastUsedAt };
        });
    },
    async markDeleted(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row && row.deletedAt === null) row.deletedAt = at;
    },
    async takeDown(userId: string, at: Date, deviceId: string | null): Promise<string[]> {
      // One transaction, as the real one: when it fails midway nothing it would have written lands.
      if (faults.has("takeDown")) throw new Error("the take-down transaction failed midway and was rolled back");
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (row && row.deletedAt === null) row.deletedAt = at;
      const revoked = takeDownRows(userId, at);
      recordEvent({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId, metadata: {} });
      return revoked;
    },
    async finishTakeDown(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      // As the real statement: only a row marked deleted and not purged yet.
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt === null || row.purgedAt !== null) return [];
      return takeDownRows(userId, at);
    },
    // 3f: no address is held in this fake, so a deleted row is always purged.
    async finishPurge(userId: string, at: Date): Promise<"purged" | "held" | "none"> {
      const row = users.get(userId);
      if (!row || row.deletedAt === null || row.purgedAt !== null) return "none";
      Object.assign(row, {
        email: `deleted:${userId}`,
        emailVerifiedAt: null,
        passwordHash: null,
        totpSecretEnc: null,
        totpEnabledAt: null,
        recoveryCodesHash: [],
        phoneHash: null,
        ageConfirmedAt: null,
        termsVersion: null,
        termsAcceptedAt: null,
        purgedAt: at,
      });
      return "purged";
    },
    // 3f: what the deletion mail reads of a held address; this fake holds none.
    async addressHold(): Promise<{ until: Date; final: boolean; told: boolean } | null> {
      return null;
    },
  } satisfies Pick<
    AuthRepo,
    | "findUserById"
    | "findUserByEmail"
    | "setPasswordFailures"
    | "createEmailCode"
    | "findEmailCode"
    | "addCodeAttempt"
    | "consumeEmailCode"
    | "changeEmail"
    | "setPasswordHash"
    | "enableTotp"
    | "disableTotp"
    | "lockDown"
    | "setPhoneHash"
    | "appendEvent"
    | "findDeviceById"
    | "ensureWebauthnUserId"
    | "countPasskeys"
    | "listPasskeys"
    | "findPasskey"
    | "recentPasskeyAdditions"
    | "addPasskey"
    | "renamePasskey"
    | "deletePasskey"
    | "findPasskeyByCredentialId"
    | "findPasskeyByCredential"
    | "claimPasskeyUse"
    | "suspectPasskey"
    | "findDevice"
    | "createDevice"
    | "touchDevice"
    | "createSession"
    | "findActiveSession"
    | "rotateSession"
    | "writeFactor"
    | "claimTotpStep"
    | "revokeAllSessions"
    | "listActiveSessions"
    | "markDeleted"
    | "takeDown"
    | "finishTakeDown"
    | "finishPurge"
    | "addressHold"
  >;
  const authRepo = repo as unknown as AuthRepo;
  const kv = new MemoryKv(() => t);
  const mailer = new MemoryMailer();
  /** profiles.verified_at by account, as the badge flows set and clear it through the profile store. */
  const verified = new Map<string, Date | null>();
  /** 3e: the accounts whose suspension runs, as the profile store's predicate would read them; a test adds to it. */
  const suspended = new Set<string>();
  const config: AuthConfig = {
    appOrigin: "http://localhost:8081",
    allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8081"],
    authHmacKey: Buffer.alloc(32, 3),
    ipHashKey: Buffer.alloc(32, 4),
    totpKey: parseVersionedKey(`v1:${Buffer.alloc(32, 5).toString("base64")}`),
    totpPreviousKeys: [],
    notifierKey: parseVersionedKey(`v1:${Buffer.alloc(32, 6).toString("base64")}`),
    notifierPreviousKeys: [],
    termsVersion: TEST_TERMS,
    trustProxy: "none",
    verifyProvider: "dev",
    webauthn: { rpId: "localhost", rpName: "korbat", origins: ["http://localhost:8081"] },
    // The staff console is off: no flow this harness runs reaches it.
    console: null,
    homeState: null,
    contactPoint: null,
    // 3f Task 5: the report hold, on as by default.
    reportHold: true,
  };
  const deps: AuthDeps = {
    repo: authRepo,
    kv,
    sessions: createSessions({ repo: authRepo, kv, now }),
    lockout: createLockout({ repo: authRepo, kv, now }),
    mailer,
    turnstile: { verify: async () => true },
    breachChecker: { isBreached: async () => false },
    // The flows this harness runs create no profile; the badge flows only set and clear verified_at, kept above by
    // account, and the deletion flow reads the handle, kept by account as `user` registers it. No flow here changes the
    // Explore switch, which reads as the column's default.
    profiles: {
      create: async () => {
        throw new Error("the memory harness has no profile store");
      },
      find: async (id) => {
        const handle = handles.get(id);
        return handle === undefined ? null : { id, handle, displayName: handle, handleChangedAt: null, verified: (verified.get(id) ?? null) !== null, showInExplore: true };
      },
      // 3e: setting the badge is refused while the account's suspension runs, as the predicate refuses the real write.
      setVerified: async (id, at) => {
        if (at !== null && suspended.has(id)) return false;
        verified.set(id, at);
        return true;
      },
      suspended: async (id) => suspended.has(id),
    },
    // The development provider, which accepts exactly 000000; a test swaps it for null or a scripted one.
    verify: devProvider(),
    config,
    log: pino({ level: "silent" }),
    now,
  };
  const ctx: RequestContext = { ipHash: randomToken(), userAgent: undefined };
  /**
   * A live session on a device of its own, both recorded as the deletion flow will find them. It proved an email code
   * just now unless given other factors, as a session behind requireFreshAuth has, and started from no passkey unless told so.
   * The device is a web browser labelled as the sign-in labels one, unless the test says otherwise.
   */
  const session = (userId: string, options: { factors?: Factors; passkeyId?: string | null; platform?: Platform; label?: string | null } = {}): Session => {
    const s: Session = {
      sessionId: sha256Hex(randomToken()),
      userId,
      deviceId: randomUUID(),
      role: "user",
      onboarded: true,
      mfaEnabled: false,
      reauthAt: now(),
      handle: randomUUID(),
      factors: options.factors ?? { email: t },
      passkeyId: options.passkeyId ?? null,
    };
    sessions.push({
      id: s.sessionId,
      userId,
      revokedAt: null,
      deviceId: s.deviceId,
      handle: s.handle,
      factors: s.factors,
      passkeyId: s.passkeyId,
      reauthAt: s.reauthAt,
      createdAt: now(),
      lastUsedAt: now(),
      expiresAt: new Date(t + SESSION_IDLE_MS),
      absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(t + SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MS),
    });
    devices.push({ id: s.deviceId, userId, revokedAt: null, platform: options.platform ?? "web", label: options.label === undefined ? "Chrome on Windows" : options.label });
    return s;
  };
  return {
    deps,
    kv,
    mailer,
    ctx,
    users,
    codes,
    events,
    sessions,
    devices,
    passkeys,
    verified,
    suspended,
    faults,
    now,
    advance(ms: number) {
      t += ms;
    },
    /** Another session of an existing account, on another device. */
    session,
    /**
     * A passkey of an existing account, created at `createdAt` (now unless given) with the row's defaults (a plain,
     * unnamed synced key added from no device) unless overridden; answers its id.
     */
    passkey(userId: string, createdAt: Date = now(), overrides: Partial<Omit<RecordedPasskey, "id" | "userId" | "createdAt">> = {}): string {
      const id = randomUUID();
      passkeys.push({
        id,
        userId,
        createdAt,
        credentialId: randomToken(),
        publicKey: "cose-key",
        counter: 0,
        transports: [],
        backedUp: false,
        name: "Passkey",
        lastUsedAt: null,
        aaguid: null,
        backupEligible: false,
        uvInitialized: false,
        createdDeviceId: null,
        suspectAt: null,
        ...overrides,
      });
      return id;
    },
    /**
     * An onboarded account holding a verified address, with a session that just proved a credential, as a route
     * behind requireFreshAuth passes it on. Its profile's handle is the address's local part unless given.
     */
    user(email: string, handle: string = email.split("@")[0]!.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_]/g, "_")): { user: UserRow; session: Session } {
      const id = randomUUID();
      const user: UserRow = {
        id,
        email,
        emailVerifiedAt: now(),
        phoneHash: null,
        passwordHash: null,
        totpSecretEnc: null,
        totpEnabledAt: null,
        recoveryCodesHash: [],
        failedLogins: 0,
        lockedUntil: null,
        createdAt: now(),
        deletedAt: null,
        role: "user",
        ageConfirmedAt: now(),
        termsVersion: TEST_TERMS,
        termsAcceptedAt: now(),
        onboardedAt: now(),
        passwordChangedAt: null,
        totpLastStep: null,
        purgedAt: null,
        webauthnUserId: null,
      };
      users.set(id, user);
      handles.set(id, handle);
      return { user, session: session(id) };
    },
  };
}

export type MemoryFlowHarness = ReturnType<typeof memoryFlowHarness>;
```

      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: "http://localhost:1025", MAIL_FROM: MAIL.MAIL_FROM }, /SMTP_URL/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, SMTP_URL: MAIL.SMTP_URL }, /MAIL_FROM/],

      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for revoke:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|CONSOLE_ORIGIN|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
    }

  test("run with a setting missing, it names it, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();

    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for revoke:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("SMTP_URL");
  });
});

describe("staff.js: the commands for moderation cases (3c design, section 7.13)", () => {
  const CASE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

  test("the usage lists them, and says which run in the migrate service", () => {
    for (const words of ["text-verify", "access-request <@handle | email>", "link <staff email> <personal handle>", "unlink <staff email> <personal handle>", "limits <decisions per hour> <decisions per day> <case opens per day> <findings per day> <reveals per day>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("linked to it");
    // 3f Task 5: notification-facts replaces account-facts, and the record commands are listed with the order commands.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).not.toContain("account-facts");
    for (const words of ["records [--verify]", "notification-facts <record>", "notification-sent <record>", "production-account <order>", "address-check --handle <handle> < address", "handover-list <seal action>", "handover-record <production>", "handover-destroyed <production>"]) {
      expect(STAFF_USAGE, words).toContain(`  ${words}`);
    }
  });

  test("3f's review: alert-test, with or without --on-call, and nothing else; and every runbook step that publishes a test names the staff.js command that does", () => {
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("  alert-test [--on-call] ");
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["alert-test"])).toEqual({ command: "alert-test", onCall: false });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["alert-test", "--on-call"])).toEqual({ command: "alert-test", onCall: true });
    for (const args of [["alert-test", "--all"], ["alert-test", "--on-call", "--on-call"]]) expect(() => parseStaffArgs(args), args.join(" ")).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);

import { createHash, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { crc32 } from "node:zlib";
import { unzipSync } from "fflate";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { MEDIA_SIZES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { isStoredName, runHandover, storedName, zipStored } from "../src/handover";
import { storedImageName } from "../src/media";

const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
const sha256 = (data: Buffer | Uint8Array) => createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex");

/**
 * The hand-over's program (3f design, section 7.14 step 2; invariant 16), as a unit: against a store of harmless files
 * that are not images, in a temporary directory. The archive's entries equal the list byte for byte and are stored, not
 * compressed; a name outside the store's layout, a missing file and a list that names a file twice are refused with no
 * archive; the printed digests are the files' and the archive's. The store's naming rule exists twice, exported by the
 * media module and copied in handover.ts: the two are fed the same names and must agree.
 */
describe("the hand-over's program", () => {
  const dirs: string[] = [];
  afterEach(() => {
    for (const dir of dirs.splice(0)) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  /** A store with these images' files, each size a few harmless bytes of its own, and an empty directory for the archive. */
  function store(ids: string[]) {
    const root = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "korbat-handover-"));
    dirs.push(root);
    const storeDir = path.join(root, "store");
    const out = path.join(root, "out");
    mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
    const files = new Map<string, Buffer>();
    for (const id of ids) {
      for (const size of MEDIA_SIZES) {
        const name = storedName(id, size);
        const data = Buffer.from(`not an image: ${size} of ${id} ${"x".repeat(size === "large" ? 300 : 30)}`, "utf8");
        mkdirSync(path.join(storeDir, ...name.split("/").slice(0, -1)), { recursive: true });
        writeFileSync(path.join(storeDir, ...name.split("/")), data);
        files.set(name, data);
      }
    }
    return { storeDir, out, files };
  }
  async function run(input: string, storeDir: string, out: string) {
    const lines: string[] = [];
    const errors: string[] = [];
    const code = await runHandover({ input, store: storeDir, out, log: (line) => lines.push(line), error: (line) => errors.push(line) });
    return { code, lines, errors };
  }

  test("the store's naming rule in its two copies: the media module's and the program's give the same names, and the program accepts exactly those", () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      const id = randomUUID();
      for (const size of MEDIA_SIZES) {
        expect(storedName(id, size)).toBe(storedImageName(id, size));
        expect(isStoredName(storedImageName(id, size))).toBe(true);
      }
    }
    const id = randomUUID();
    const other = randomUUID();
    for (const name of [
      `files/${other.slice(0, 2) === id.slice(0, 2) ? "zz" : other.slice(0, 2)}/${id}/small.webp`,
      `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/${id}/huge.webp`,
      `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/${id.toUpperCase()}/small.webp`,
      `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/../../${id}/small.webp`,
      `/etc/passwd`,
      `results/${id}.json`,
      `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/${id}/small.webp/x`,
      `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/${id}/small.webp${String.fromCharCode(0)}`,
      `files${String.fromCharCode(92)}${id.slice(0, 2)}${String.fromCharCode(92)}${id}${String.fromCharCode(92)}small.webp`,
      "",
    ]) {
      expect(isStoredName(name), JSON.stringify(name)).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(() => storedName("not-an-id", "small")).toThrow();
    expect(() => storedImageName("not-an-id", "small")).toThrow();
  });

  test("copies exactly the listed files, byte for byte, into one archive of stored entries, and prints each file's and the archive's size and SHA-256", async () => {
    const ids = [randomUUID(), randomUUID()];
    const s = store(ids);
    const production = randomUUID();
    const names = [...s.files.keys()];
    const done = await run([`production ${production}`, ...names, ""].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect(done.errors).toEqual([]);
    expect(done.code).toBe(0);
    const archivePath = path.join(s.out, `handover-${production}.zip`);
    const archive = readFileSync(archivePath);
    expect(done.lines).toEqual([...names.map((name) => `${name} ${s.files.get(name)!.length} ${sha256(s.files.get(name)!)}`), `archive ${archive.length} ${sha256(archive)}`]);
    // A ZIP reader finds exactly the listed entries, with the files' bytes.
    const entries = unzipSync(new Uint8Array(archive));
    expect(Object.keys(entries)).toEqual(names);
    for (const name of names) expect(Buffer.from(entries[name]!)).toEqual(s.files.get(name));
    // Each local header: stored (method 0), with the file's own CRC-32 and size twice, then the bytes as they are.
    let at = 0;
    for (const name of names) {
      const data = s.files.get(name)!;
      expect(archive.readUInt32LE(at)).toBe(0x04034b50);
      expect(archive.readUInt16LE(at + 8)).toBe(0);
      expect(archive.readUInt32LE(at + 14)).toBe(crc32(data));
      expect([archive.readUInt32LE(at + 18), archive.readUInt32LE(at + 22)]).toEqual([data.length, data.length]);
      const nameLength = archive.readUInt16LE(at + 26);
      expect(archive.subarray(at + 30, at + 30 + nameLength).toString("utf8")).toBe(name);
      expect(archive.subarray(at + 30 + nameLength, at + 30 + nameLength + data.length)).toEqual(data);
      at += 30 + nameLength + data.length;
    }
    // A second run never overwrites the archive of the first.
    const again = await run([`production ${production}`, ...names].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect(again.code).toBe(1);
    expect(again.lines).toEqual([]);
    expect(readFileSync(archivePath)).toEqual(archive);
  });

  test("refuses a name outside the store's layout, a missing file, a list without its production and a file named twice, each with no archive", async () => {
    const id = randomUUID();
    const s = store([id]);
    const production = randomUUID();
    const target = path.join(s.out, `handover-${production}.zip`);
    const names = [...s.files.keys()];
    const outside = await run([`production ${production}`, names[0], "../../outside.webp"].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect([outside.code, outside.lines, outside.errors]).toEqual([1, [], ['handover: refused: "../../outside.webp" is outside the store']]);
    const missing = storedName(randomUUID(), "small");
    const gone = await run([`production ${production}`, names[0], missing].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect([gone.code, gone.lines, gone.errors]).toEqual([1, [], [`handover: ${missing} is missing or is not a plain file of the store; no archive was written`]]);
    expect((await run(names.join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out)).code).toBe(1);
    expect((await run([`production ${production}`, names[0], names[0]].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out)).code).toBe(1);
    // A directory where a file should be is no plain file either.
    const dirId = randomUUID();
    mkdirSync(path.join(s.storeDir, ...storedName(dirId, "small").split("/")), { recursive: true });
    expect((await run([`production ${production}`, storedName(dirId, "small")].join(LF), s.storeDir, s.out)).code).toBe(1);
    expect(existsSync(target)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("3f's review: a write that fails halfway leaves no part of the files behind and says so; an earlier run's file, whole or not, is never overwritten and must be deleted first", async () => {
    const id = randomUUID();
    const s = store([id]);
    const production = randomUUID();
    const input = [`production ${production}`, ...s.files.keys()].join(LF);
    const name = `handover-${production}.zip`;
    // A full disk: half the archive is written, then the write fails.
    const errors: string[] = [];
    const failing = await runHandover({
      input,
      store: s.storeDir,
      out: s.out,
      log: () => undefined,
      error: (line) => errors.push(line),
      writeArchive: async (file, data) => {
        await file.write(data.subarray(0, Math.floor(data.length / 2)));
        throw Object.assign(new Error("no space left on device"), { code: "ENOSPC" });
      },
    });
    expect(failing).toBe(1);
    expect(errors).toEqual([`handover: ${name} could not be written (ENOSPC); what was written of it was deleted, and no archive was written`]);
    expect(readdirSync(s.out)).toEqual([]);
    // An earlier run's archive stands: the next run refuses, says what to do, and leaves it as it was.
    writeFileSync(path.join(s.out, name), "an earlier run's bytes");
    const again = await run(input, s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect([again.code, again.lines]).toEqual([1, []]);
    expect(again.errors).toEqual([`handover: ${name} or ${name}.part exists from an earlier run; it may be incomplete and holds the files it lists: delete it before running again; what was written of it was deleted`]);
    expect(readFileSync(path.join(s.out, name), "utf8")).toBe("an earlier run's bytes");
    expect(readdirSync(s.out)).toEqual([name]);
    // An earlier run's part, left by a run that was killed: refused before anything is written.
    rmSync(path.join(s.out, name));
    writeFileSync(path.join(s.out, `${name}.part`), "half");
    const killed = await run(input, s.storeDir, s.out);
    expect([killed.code, killed.errors]).toEqual([1, [`handover: ${name} or ${name}.part exists from an earlier run; it may be incomplete and holds the files it lists: delete it before running again; no archive was written`]]);
    // Once it is deleted, the run writes the archive under its name alone.
    rmSync(path.join(s.out, `${name}.part`));
    expect((await run(input, s.storeDir, s.out)).code).toBe(0);
    expect(readdirSync(s.out)).toEqual([name]);
  });

  test("the zip writer: an empty file and a name of several bytes a character, read back by a reader, with CRC-32s from node:zlib", () => {
    const files = [
      { name: "files/aa/empty", data: Buffer.alloc(0) },
      { name: `files/${String.fromCodePoint(0xe9)}/two`, data: Buffer.from([0, 1, 2, 255]) },
    ];
    const archive = zipStored(files);
    const entries = unzipSync(new Uint8Array(archive));
    expect(Object.keys(entries)).toEqual(files.map((file) => file.name));
    expect(Buffer.from(entries[files[1]!.name]!)).toEqual(files[1]!.data);
    expect(archive.readUInt32LE(14)).toBe(crc32(files[0]!.data));
    // The end record counts both entries.
    expect(archive.readUInt32LE(archive.length - 22)).toBe(0x06054b50);
    expect(archive.readUInt16LE(archive.length - 12)).toBe(2);
  });
});

import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ORDER_RULES, renderAlert, type AlertFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { StaffMessage } from "../../src/auth";
import { alertMailLeg, alertTick, channelHealth, staffAlert } from "../../src/moderation/alerts";
import { overview } from "../../src/moderation/cases";
import { CHANNEL_TABLES, rowCounts } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { noticesWorld, type NoticesWorld } from "./notices-harness";
import { ageMessageForTest, closeNotifyFixtures, contactMessageForTest, nextValidity, outboxOf, outboxSince, removeMessages, type OutboxRow } from "./notify-fixtures";
import { newStaffKey, newStaffSession, rolledBack } from "./staff-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 60_000 });

const MIN = 60_000;

/**
 * The alert channel's time-driven alerts and its two legs (3f design, sections 6.1, 7.2 and 12.1; invariants 14 and 15):
 * alert_steps() writes an escalation at escalate_minutes and the deadline's two reminders, each once, and stops them when
 * the message is handled; a person already at work in the console is not absent; the daily test is written once a day.
 * The alert tick mails every row whose mail is its sentence once, never one of 3c's or 3e's kinds, and with NOTIFY on
 * judges the channel's health with its own alarms, once in 24 hours. staffAlert writes the row of every kind of 3c and
 * 3e and marks it mailed either way.
 *
 * The steps run inside transactions of the migrator that end in a rollback: there the test sets the times it needs and
 * pushes every staff session back a day, so that the sessions earlier files of the run opened do not count as someone at
 * work. The tick commits, as the server's does; its rows and messages are removed by id, and the file's last test holds
 * it to leaving no row behind.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: the alert steps and the alert tick", () => {
  let w: NoticesWorld;
  let staffEmail: string;
  let before: Record<string, number>;
  const made: string[] = [];
  const started = new Date();

  beforeAll(async () => {
    w = noticesWorld();
    before = await rowCounts(w.apiDb, CHANNEL_TABLES);
    // A live staff account with a key and a session: the address the staff mails of this file go to, and a session a
    // test can mark as used.
    const staff = await newStaffKey(w.authDb, w.migrateDb, w.repo, "moderator");
    staffEmail = staff.user.email;
    await newStaffSession(w.authDb, staff.user.id, staff.key.id);
    await w.migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.notify_state`);
  }, 60_000);
  afterEach(async () => {
    await removeMessages(w.migrateDb, made.splice(0));
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await w.migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.notify_state`);
    await closeNotifyFixtures();
    await w.close();
  });

  /** A message inside the migrator's transaction, received `minutes` ago: the migrator keeps the time it supplies. */
  const messageIn = async (tx: DbTx, minutes: number, extra: { stale?: boolean } = {}) => {
    const [row] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
      insert into public.contact_messages (folder, uidvalidity, uid, received_at, seen_at, stale)
      values ('inbox', ${nextValidity()}, 1, now() - make_interval(mins => ${minutes}), now() - make_interval(mins => ${minutes}), ${extra.stale ?? false}) returning id`);
    return row!.id;
  };
  /** Every staff session pushed a day back, its lifetime with it: nobody is at work in the console. */
  const nobodyAtWork = (tx: DbTx) =>
    tx.execute(sql`update auth.staff_sessions set created_at = created_at - interval '1 day', last_used_at = last_used_at - interval '1 day', idle_expires_at = idle_expires_at - interval '1 day', absolute_expires_at = absolute_expires_at - interval '1 day'`);
  const steps = async (tx: DbTx) => Number((await tx.execute<{ written: number }>(sql`select public.alert_steps() as written`))[0]!.written);
  const kinds = (rows: OutboxRow[]) => rows.map((r) => [r.kind, r.step]);

  test("an unanswered message is escalated to every phone once, escalate_minutes after it arrived, and not before", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      await nobodyAtWork(tx);
      const early = await messageIn(tx, ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes - 1);
      const due = await messageIn(tx, ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes + 1);
      await steps(tx);
      expect(kinds((await outboxOf(tx, early)).filter((r) => r.kind === "contact_mail_escalated"))).toEqual([]);
      const escalated = (await outboxOf(tx, due)).filter((r) => r.kind === "contact_mail_escalated");
      expect(kinds(escalated)).toEqual([["contact_mail_escalated", 0]]);
      expect([escalated[0]!.priority, escalated[0]!.scope]).toEqual([5, "all"]);
      expect(Object.keys(escalated[0]!.facts).sort()).toEqual(["dueAt", "receivedAt"]);
      // Once a message: a second call writes nothing for it.
      await steps(tx);
      expect((await outboxOf(tx, due)).filter((r) => r.kind === "contact_mail_escalated")).toHaveLength(1);
    });

  test("order_due for a message: one row at remind_minutes and one at the deadline, each once, with the deadline and the minutes left", async () => {

      // Past the deadline only the deadline's row: the later of the two that has passed.
      expect((await due(late)).map((r) => [r.step, r.facts.minutesLeft])).toEqual([[0, 0]]);
      // Each once: a second call writes nothing; the deadline's row comes when the deadline passes.

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- the tick

  const tickDeps = (notify: "on" | "off") => ({ ...w.deps, config: { ...w.deps.config, NOTIFY: notify } });
  /** One round of each of the two jobs, the tick and (a job of its own since 3f's review) its mail leg: the tick's report. */
  const round = async (notify: "on" | "off") => {
    const report = await alertTick(tickDeps(notify));
    await alertMailLeg(tickDeps(notify));
    return report;
  };
  const mailsOf = (template: string) => w.mailer.to(staffEmail, template);

  test("the tick's mail leg mails a row whose mail is its sentence once, to every staff account, and marks it", async () => {

    expect(row!.mailed_at).not.toBeNull();
    const mails = mailsOf("contact_mail").slice(sent);
    expect(mails).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(mails[0]!.data).toMatchObject({ receivedAt: row!.facts.receivedAt, dueAt: row!.facts.dueAt });
    // Mailed once: the next round finds nothing owed.
    await round("off");
    expect(mailsOf("contact_mail").slice(sent)).toHaveLength(1);
  });
