```ts
      expect(await item()).toMatchObject({ running: false, preserved: false, frozen: false });
      view(await correct(tx, admin, order.id, { kind: "tco_removal" }, true));
      expect(await item()).toEqual(preserved);
    });
  });

  /**
   * The race of a correction that closes an item with "Disable for an order" on the same order (section 5, items 1 and
   * 2), on committed rows: a third session holds a row the effect or the correction must wait for, for a moment. The
   * effect runs in a transaction that is rolled back at its end, as the made-up confirmation asks; the correction commits.
   */
  async function race(hold: "case" | "item"): Promise<{ effect: string; correction: string; closed: string | null }> {
    const authors: string[] = [];
    const made = [await imagePost(w.apiDb, 0), await imagePost(w.apiDb, 0)].sort((a, b) => (a.postId < b.postId ? -1 : 1));
    for (const m of made) authors.push(m.authorId);
    // A report keeps a case open on the second post, which the effect takes before the order's row.
    const reporter = await newProfile(w.apiDb);
    authors.push(reporter.id);
    const caseId = (await intake(w.apiDb, ground.rule(reporter.id), aPost(made[1]!.postId))).items[0]!.caseId!;
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: made.map((m) => m.postId) });
    orders.push(order.id);
    const first = order.items.find((item) => item.postId === made[0]!.postId)!;
    let effect = "none";
    let correction = "none";
    try {
      let release!: () => void;
      const released = new Promise<void>((resolve) => (release = resolve));
      const holder = w.migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '20s'`);
        if (hold === "case") await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from public.cases where id = ${caseId}::uuid for update`);
        else await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from public.legal_order_items where id = ${first.id}::uuid for update`);
        await released;
      });
      await sleep(200);
      const runEffect = () =>
        w.apiDb
          .transaction(async (tx) => {
            try {
              const done = await effectWith(tx, moderator, order.id, effectParams(order));
              effect = done.items.map((item) => (item.inForce ? "in force" : item.closedAt !== null ? "closed" : "open")).join(",");
            } catch (err) {
              effect = err instanceof ModerationError ? err.code : `${String(err)} ${String((err as { cause?: unknown }).cause)}`;
            }
            throw new Error("the effect's transaction is rolled back");
          })
          .catch(() => undefined);
      const runCorrection = async () => {
        const outcome = await correct(w.apiDb, admin, order.id, { closeItems: [{ itemId: first.id, reason: "no_post" }] });
        correction = typeof outcome === "string" ? outcome : "corrected";
      };
      // With the case held, the effect starts first and waits on the second post's case holding the first item; with the
      // item held, the correction starts first and waits for it, and the effect after it.
      const [a, b] = hold === "case" ? [runEffect, runCorrection] : [runCorrection, runEffect];
      const started = [a()];
      await sleep(800);
      started.push(b());
      await sleep(800);
      release();
      await holder;
      await Promise.all(started);
      const [row] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ reason: string | null }>(sql`select closed_reason as reason from public.legal_order_items where id = ${first.id}::uuid`);
      return { effect, correction, closed: row!.reason };
    } finally {
      await removeFixtures(w.migrateDb, authors);
    }
  }

  test("a correction that closes an item meets an effect on the same order: never a deadlock; it waits for the effect and is refused, or commits first and the effect is refused", async () => {
    // The effect holds the first item and waits for the second post's case; the correction comes then. The correction
    // waits for the first item before it takes the order's row, so the effect goes on to the end; the correction then
    // closes the first item, which the rolled-back effect left open.
    const effectFirst = await race("case");
    expect(effectFirst).toEqual({ effect: "in force,in force", correction: "corrected", closed: "no_post" });
    // The correction holds the order's items first and closes the first one; the effect, which read the order before,
    // then holds that item and finds it closed: it gives effect to nothing (order_changed), and the closing stands.
    const correctionFirst = await race("item");
    expect(correctionFirst).toEqual({ effect: "order_changed", correction: "corrected", closed: "no_post" });
  });

  test("leaves no row behind", async () => {
    await removeOrders(w.migrateDb, orders.splice(0));
    await removeMessages(w.migrateDb, messages.splice(0));
    await removeOrderAlerts(w.migrateDb, started);
    expect(await rowCounts(w.apiDb, [...ORDER_TABLES, ...CHANNEL_TABLES])).toEqual(before);
  });
});
```

```ts
 * alert, and 28). With Section C the notice is held: nothing reaches the author, and a decision of korbat's own about
 * the post taken during the hold is held with it, while its reporter is answered as always. order_notices_release()
 * tells nothing before the hold's end and everything at it, stamping clock_timestamp(); a correction that holds the

    const reported = await intake(w.apiDb, ground.rule(reporter.id), aPost(p.postId));
    const caseId = reported.items[0]!.caseId!;
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });
    const done = await effect(order);
    const decisionId = done.items[0]!.decisionId!;
    expect(await told(decisionId)).toMatchObject({ informed: false, mail: "none" });
    // During the hold a removal under a rule: recorded, held, and its reporter's item answered.
    const removal = await world.decideAs(moderator, caseId, { kind: "final", actions: [act("remove")] });
    if (typeof removal === "string") throw new Error(removal);
    expect(await told(removal.decisionId)).toMatchObject({ informed: false, mail: "none" });
    const [item] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ answered: boolean }>(sql`select answered_by is not null as answered from public.intake_items where case_id = ${caseId}::uuid and reporter_account_id = ${reporter.id}::uuid`);
    expect(item!.answered).toBe(true);
    // Nothing on the author's side: no row, no screen, no chip, no export entry.
    const deps = { apiDb: w.apiDb };
    expect((await authorCases(deps, p.authorId)).decisions).toEqual([]);
    await expect(authorDecisionView(deps, p.authorId, decisionId)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ModerationError);
    await expect(authorDecisionView(deps, p.authorId, removal.decisionId)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ModerationError);
    expect((await authorFacts(deps, p.authorId, [p.postId])).size).toBe(0);
    expect(await exportedDecisions(deps, p.authorId)).toEqual([]);
    // The removal gave a strike, which counts nowhere the author can see while it is held: not on Cases' "Your
    // standing", not in /api/me's standing, not in the export's strikes (section 7.10); the release counts it.
    const [struck] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.decision_actions where decision_id = ${removal.decisionId}::uuid and kind = 'strike'`);
    expect(struck!.n).toBe(1);
    const strikes = async () => [(await authorCases(deps, p.authorId)).activeStrikes, (await standingFor(w.apiDb, p.authorId))?.activeStrikes, (await exportedStrikes(w.apiDb, p.authorId)).length];
    expect(await strikes()).toEqual([0, 0, 0]);
    // The API role cannot write a decision's informed_at.
    const refused = await w.apiDb.execute(sql`update public.decisions set informed_at = now() where id = ${decisionId}::uuid`).then(
      () => "written",
      () => "refused",
    );
    expect(refused).toBe("refused");
    // Before the end, nothing is told; an end a moment ahead, and at it everything is.
    expect(await release()).toBe(0);
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set authority_hold_until = clock_timestamp() + make_interval(secs => 2) where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
    expect(await release()).toBe(0);
    const [end] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ until: string }>(sql`select to_char(public.order_hold_until(${order.id}::uuid) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as until`);
    await sleep(2_200);
    expect(await release()).toBe(2);
    const order_told = await told(decisionId);
    expect(order_told).toMatchObject({ informed: true, mail: "pending" });
    // Never before the end: the stamp is the clock's at the release.
    expect(Date.parse(order_told.informed_at!)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(Date.parse(end!.until));
    expect(await told(removal.decisionId)).toMatchObject({ informed: true, mail: "pending" });
    expect(await strikes()).toEqual([1, 1, 1]);
    const [event] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.legal_order_events where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid and kind = 'notice_released' and via = 'system'`);
    expect(event!.n).toBe(1);
    // Now the author reads both, and the notice says that it was held until now.
    expect((await authorCases(deps, p.authorId)).decisions.map((d) => [d.kind, d.order ?? null])).toEqual([
      ["final", null],
      ["order", "disabled"],
    ]);
    const view = await authorDecisionView(deps, p.authorId, decisionId);
    expect(view.content).toBeNull();
    // korbat's own removal, held and released with the notice, shows the still disabled post no more than the notice does.
    expect((await authorDecisionView(deps, p.authorId, removal.decisionId)).content).toBeNull();
    expect(view.appealUntil).toBeNull();
    expect(view.order).toMatchObject({ held: true, kind: "tco_removal", withholdAuthor: true });
    expect(statementParagraphs(view, { texts: view.orderTexts ?? null }).join(" ")).toContain("korbat was not allowed to tell you until now.");
    // The chip: a disabled post has none (its level is disabled, which no list shows).
    expect((await authorFacts(deps, p.authorId, [p.postId])).size).toBe(0);
    // A second release tells nothing more.
    expect(await release()).toBe(0);
  });

  test("a measure never rests on a decision its subject has not been told of: a suspension at once on a threat found in the held post is refused, and allowed once the threat's removal is told", async () => {
    // As the migrator, who alone may end the hold by hand here; the flows run as they do for the API.
    await rolledBack(world.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const author = await newProfile(tx as unknown as Db);
      const p = await imagePost(tx, 0, author.id);
      const order = await orderForTest(tx, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });
      await effectWith(tx, moderator, order.id, effectParams(order));
      // An admin's own finding of a direct threat in the disabled post, decided as a removal: held with the notice.
      const finding = await intake(tx, ground.finding(admin.id, "R5"), aPost(p.postId));
      const threat = await decideIn(tx, admin, finding.items[0]!.caseId!, { kind: "final", ruleId: "R5", actions: [act("remove")] });
      const [held] = await tx.execute<{ informed: boolean }>(sql`select informed_at is not null as informed from public.decisions where id = ${threat}::uuid`);
      expect(held!.informed).toBe(false);
      // The suspension at once on the threat basis would be told at once, on the account's case: no basis while it is held.
      const onAccount = await intake(tx, ground.finding(admin.id, "R5"), anAccount(author.id, author.handle));
      const suspend = () => decideIn(tx, admin, onAccount.items[0]!.caseId!, { kind: "final", ruleId: "R5", actions: [timed("suspend", 7, false)] });
      expect(await refusal(suspend())).toBe("invalid_decision");
      // Once the hold has ended and the release has told the threat's removal, the same suspension rests on it.
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = now(), hold_end_reason = 'released_by_authority' where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
      await tx.execute(sql`select public.order_notices_release()`);
      const suspension = await suspend();
      const [rests] = await tx.execute<{ basis: string; rests: string[] }>(sql`select basis, rests_on::text[] as rests from public.decision_actions where decision_id = ${suspension}::uuid and kind = 'suspend'`);
      expect([rests!.basis, rests!.rests]).toEqual(["threat", [threat]]);
    });
  });

  test("a second order on a post whose notice another order holds is held with it, and both are told at the first order's release", async () => {
    // As the migrator, who alone may end the hold by hand here; the flows run as they do for the API.
    await rolledBack(world.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const p = await imagePost(tx, 0);
      const a = await orderForTest(tx, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true, reference: `A-${p.postId}` });
      const first = (await effectWith(tx, moderator, a.id, effectParams(a))).items[0]!.decisionId!;
      // B asks for no silence, but its notice would say that another decision already keeps the post from being shown.
      const b = await orderForTest(tx, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], reference: `B-${p.postId}` });
      const second = (await effectWith(tx, moderator, b.id, effectParams(b))).items[0]!.decisionId!;
      const state = async (id: string) =>
        (await tx.execute<{ informed: boolean; mail: string }>(sql`select informed_at is not null as informed, author_mail::text as mail from public.decisions where id = ${id}::uuid`))[0]!;
      expect([await state(first), await state(second)]).toEqual([
        { informed: false, mail: "none" },
        { informed: false, mail: "none" },
      ]);
      const releaseIn = async () => (await tx.execute<{ told: number }>(sql`select public.order_notices_release() as told`))[0]!.told;
      expect(await releaseIn()).toBe(0);
      expect(await state(second)).toEqual({ informed: false, mail: "none" });
      // A's hold ends: one release tells both.
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = now(), hold_end_reason = 'released_by_authority' where id = ${a.id}::uuid`);
      expect(await releaseIn()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
      expect([await state(first), await state(second)]).toEqual([
        { informed: true, mail: "pending" },
        { informed: true, mail: "pending" },
      ]);
    });
  });

  test("the release waits for a transaction that holds an untold order decision's row, and then tells it", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });
    const done = await effect(order);
    const decisionId = done.items[0]!.decisionId!;
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = now(), hold_end_reason = 'released_by_authority' where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
    let finished = false;
    let releasing: Promise<number> | null = null;
    await w.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      // What a correction of the order decision takes first.
      await tx.execute(sql`select 1 from public.decisions where id = ${decisionId}::uuid for share`);
      releasing = release().then((n) => {
        finished = true;
        return n;
      });
      await sleep(500);
      expect(finished).toBe(false);
    });
    expect(await releasing!).toBe(1);
    expect(await told(decisionId)).toMatchObject({ informed: true, mail: "pending" });
  });

  test("the authority's words recorded after the author was told make the notice's mail owed again, as order_notice_added, with the record's time; on a held notice nothing is mailed and the release's time counts", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId] });
    const done = await effect(order);
    const decisionId = done.items[0]!.decisionId!;
    // The first mail went (no address takes one here): what the dispatch round records.
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`update public.decisions set author_mail = 'sent', author_mail_at = now() where id = ${decisionId}::uuid`);
    const recorded = await cli(["order-texts", order.id, "--reasons"], "Les motifs de l'autorite.");
    expect(recorded.code).toBe(0);
    expect(recorded.text).toContain("1 authors are sent an email that the notice has grown");
    expect(await told(decisionId)).toMatchObject({ informed: true, mail: "pending" });
    const found = (await decisionStatement(w.apiDb, decisionId))!;
    expect(mailTemplateOf(found.statement, [], found.decision.authorMailAt !== null).template).toBe("order_notice_added");
    const notice = (await orderNoticeOf(w.apiDb, decisionId, "DE"))!;
    const [event] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ at: string }>(sql`select to_char(max(at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as at from public.legal_order_events where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid and kind = 'texts_recorded'`);
    expect([notice.texts.reasons, notice.texts.textsAt]).toEqual(["Les motifs de l'autorite.", event!.at]);
    // A held notice: the record changes no mail, and at the release the author holds the words from the release.
    const q = await post();
    const held = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [q.postId], sectionC: true });
    const heldDone = await effect(held);
    const heldDecision = heldDone.items[0]!.decisionId!;

    expect(quiet.text).toContain("The notice is held: it will show the text once it is released");
    expect(await told(heldDecision)).toMatchObject({ informed: false, mail: "none" });
    expect((await cli(["order-hold-end", held.id, "--reason", "released_by_authority", "--how", "the authority's letter"])).code).toBe(0);
    expect(await release()).toBe(1);
    const afterRelease = (await orderNoticeOf(w.apiDb, heldDecision, "DE"))!;
    expect(afterRelease.texts.textsAt).toBe(afterRelease.facts.informedAt);
    expect(statementParagraphs((await decisionStatement(w.apiDb, heldDecision))!.statement, { texts: afterRelease.texts }).join(" ")).not.toContain("korbat added the authority's words");
  });

  test("the notice holds the authority's reasons from the record of the reasons, not of a later text: the remedies recorded a day later move textsAt and leave reasonsAt", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    // A cross-border removal order, whose notice says since when it holds the reasons (TCO Art. 4(4)).
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], memberState: "FR" });
    const done = await effect(order);

    expect((await cli(["order-texts", order.id, "--redress"], "Les voies de recours.")).code).toBe(0);

      (await w.apiDb.execute<{ at: string }>(sql`select to_char(at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as at from public.legal_order_events
                                                  where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid and kind = 'texts_recorded' and ground = ${ground}`))[0]!.at;
    const notice = (await orderNoticeOf(w.apiDb, decisionId, "DE"))!;
    expect([notice.texts.reasonsAt, notice.texts.textsAt]).toEqual([await at("reasons"), await at("redress")]);
    const paragraphs = statementParagraphs((await decisionStatement(w.apiDb, decisionId))!.statement, { texts: notice.texts }).join(" ");
    expect(paragraphs).toContain(ORDER_NOTICE.reasonsAt(`${(await at("reasons")).slice(0, 10)} ${(await at("reasons")).slice(11, 16)} UTC`));

  test("the hold's commands: one extension of 42 days, refused a second time and after the release; a DSA order's end is the authority's, and with none nothing is released; ending a hold tells at the next round", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });
    const done = await effect(order);
    const until = async (id: string) => (await w.apiDb.execute<{ until: string | null }>(sql`select public.order_hold_until(${id}::uuid)::text as until`))[0]!.until;
    const first = await until(order.id);
    const extended = await cli(["order-hold-extend", order.id, "--received", new Date(Date.now() - 60_000).toISOString(), "--how", "the authority's reasoned decision"]);
    expect(extended.code).toBe(0);
    const [days] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ days: number }>(sql`select extract(day from public.order_hold_until(${order.id}::uuid) - ${first}::timestamptz)::int as days`);
    expect(days!.days).toBe(ORDER_RULES.holdExtensionDays);
    const again = await cli(["order-hold-extend", order.id, "--received", new Date(Date.now() - 60_000).toISOString(), "--how", "again"]);
    expect([again.code, again.text]).toEqual([1, expect.stringContaining("already extended once")]);
    // Ended as korbat's own mistake is refused while the first period of an extended hold runs; another reason ends it.
    expect((await cli(["order-hold-end", order.id, "--reason", "not_ordered", "--how", "x"])).code).toBe(1);
    expect((await cli(["order-hold-end", order.id, "--reason", "annulled", "--how", "the court's ruling"])).code).toBe(0);
    expect(await release()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(await told(done.items[0]!.decisionId!)).toMatchObject({ informed: true });
    const late = await cli(["order-hold-extend", order.id, "--received", new Date(Date.now() - 60_000).toISOString(), "--how", "late"]);
    expect([late.code, late.text]).toEqual([1, expect.stringContaining("already released")]);
    // A DSA order whose author must not be told, given effect as urgent by an admin: no end until the authority names one.
    const d = await post();
    const dsa = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, admin, { kind: "dsa_art9", posts: [d.postId], sectionC: true });
    const urgent = await effectForTest(world, admin, dsa.id, { ...effectParams(dsa), urgent: true });
    if (typeof urgent === "string") throw new Error(urgent);
    expect(await until(dsa.id)).toBe("infinity");
    expect((await cli(["order-hold-extend", dsa.id, "--received", new Date().toISOString(), "--how", "x"])).code).toBe(1);
    expect(await release()).toBe(0);
    const named = await cli(["order-hold-until", dsa.id, new Date(Date.now() + 90 * 86_400_000).toISOString(), "--basis", "the order's sentence 3", "--how", "read in the order"]);
    expect(named.code).toBe(0);
    expect(named.text).toContain("held until");
    expect(await release()).toBe(0);
    // An end in the past changes nothing without --release.
    const past = await cli(["order-hold-until", dsa.id, new Date(Date.now() - 60_000).toISOString(), "--basis", "b", "--how", "h"]);
    expect([past.code, past.text]).toEqual([1, expect.stringContaining("give --release")]);
  });

  test("the dispatch round releases what a hold no longer keeps before its statements, with one audit row order_notices_released by the system", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });

    const report = await dispatchRound(world.moderation.deps, new MemoryJobLock());
    expect(report.noticesReleased).toBe(1);
    const [audit] = await w.apiDb.execute<{ actor_id: string; metadata: { count: number } }>(

  test("hold_ending warns every staff account daily in the last days before a hold's end, and not before", async () => {
    const p = await post();
    const order = await orderForTest(w.apiDb, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC: true });
    await effect(order);
    const since = new Date();
    // The other held notices of this file end later than the warning's days; this one ends sooner.
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set authority_hold_until = now() + make_interval(days => ${ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays + 3}) where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.alert_outbox where kind = 'hold_ending'`);
    await w.apiDb.execute(sql`select public.alert_steps()`);
    const none = await outboxSince(world.migrateDb, "hold_ending", since);
    await world.migrateDb.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set authority_hold_until = now() + make_interval(days => 2) where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
    await w.apiDb.execute(sql`select public.alert_steps()`);
    const warned = await outboxSince(world.migrateDb, "hold_ending", since);
    expect(none).toEqual([]);
    expect(warned).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(warned[0]!.facts.count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect([warned[0]!.priority, warned[0]!.scope]).toEqual([3, "all"]);
    await w.apiDb.execute(sql`select public.alert_steps()`);
    expect((await outboxSince(world.migrateDb, "hold_ending", since)).length).toBe(warned.length);
    // The notice's words of the hold do not depend on its own warning.
    expect(ORDER_NOTICE.heldUntilNow.tco_removal("a", "b")).toContain("must not be told");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("order-hold-end");
  });
});
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import pino from "pino";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { ORDER_DRAFTS, type OrderView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ORDER_NOTICE, statementParagraphs } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { createMediaRepo } from "../../src/media/repo";
import { afterDecision } from "../../src/moderation/decide";
import { decisionStatement, mailTemplateOf } from "../../src/moderation/statement";
import { CHANNEL_TABLES, decideIn, imagePost, moderationDeps, newTestStaff, removeFixtures, rowCounts, staffProfile, type TestStaff } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { noticesWorld, type NoticesWorld } from "./notices-harness";
import { closeNotifyFixtures } from "./notify-fixtures";
import { ORDER_TABLES, effectWith, effectParams, orderForTest } from "./orders-fixtures";
import { rolledBack } from "./staff-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 120_000 });

/**
 * The reinstatement after an order (3f design, sections 6.3 and 7.9; invariants 6 and 25's correction after effect). An
 * admin corrects the order decision with reinstate_by_order and its ground: the measure lifted, the item reinstated and
 * its preservation ended, the event reinstated with the ground, the level derived again. Told when the disabling was
 * told, with the mail order_reinstated_notice and the notice's reinstatement paragraphs; held, and told with the notice
 * at the release, when the notice is still held. Every staff account hears of it (order_reinstated). Every test runs in a
 * transaction that is rolled back.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: reinstating after an order", () => {
  let w: NoticesWorld;
  let moderator: TestStaff;
  let admin: TestStaff;
  let before: Record<string, number>;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    w = noticesWorld();
    moderator = await newTestStaff(w.authDb, w.migrateDb, w.repo, "moderator");
    admin = await newTestStaff(w.authDb, w.migrateDb, w.repo, "admin");
    await staffProfile(w.apiDb, moderator);
    await staffProfile(w.apiDb, admin);
    before = await rowCounts(w.apiDb, [...ORDER_TABLES, ...CHANNEL_TABLES]);
  }, 60_000);
  afterAll(async () => {
    expect(await rowCounts(w.apiDb, [...ORDER_TABLES, ...CHANNEL_TABLES])).toEqual(before);
    await removeFixtures(w.migrateDb, [moderator.id, admin.id]);
    await closeNotifyFixtures();
    await w.close();
  });

  async function given(tx: DbTx, sectionC = false): Promise<{ view: OrderView; postId: string; authorId: string; mediaIds: string[] }> {
    const p = await imagePost(tx, 1);
    const order = await orderForTest(tx, moderator, { posts: [p.postId], sectionC });
    return { view: await effectWith(tx, moderator, order.id, effectParams(order)), postId: p.postId, authorId: p.authorId, mediaIds: p.mediaIds };
  }
  const reinstate = (tx: DbTx, view: OrderView, ground: keyof typeof ORDER_DRAFTS.reinstate = "withdrawn") =>
    decideIn(tx, admin, view.items[0]!.caseId!, { kind: "correction", reviewsDecisionId: view.items[0]!.decisionId!, outcome: "reversed", actions: [{ kind: "reinstate_by_order", orderGround: ground }] });
  const row = async (tx: DbTx, id: string) =>
    (await tx.execute<{ informed: boolean; told_now: boolean; mail: string; needs_admin: boolean }>(
      sql`select informed_at is not null as informed, informed_at = decided_at as told_now, author_mail::text as mail, needs_admin from public.decisions where id = ${id}::uuid`,
    ))[0]!;

  test("a told disabling is reinstated by an admin: lifted, reinstated with its ground, the post shown again, told at once with order_reinstated_notice, and every staff account alerted", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.apiDb, async (tx) => {
      const { view, postId, authorId, mediaIds } = await given(tx);
      // The disabled post's image is in no data export (W.7); the reinstatement hands it back with the post.
      const exported = createMediaRepo(tx as unknown as Db);
      expect(await exported.readyImages(authorId)).not.toContain(mediaIds[0]);
      const correction = await reinstate(tx, view, "not_authentic");
      expect(await exported.readyImages(authorId)).toContain(mediaIds[0]);
      expect(await exported.isExportable(authorId, mediaIds[0]!)).toBe(true);
      expect(await row(tx, correction)).toEqual({ informed: true, told_now: true, mail: "pending", needs_admin: true });

      expect([post!.level, post!.state]).toEqual(["visible", "visible"]);
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import {
  NOTIFICATION_ANSWERS,
  NOTIFICATION_DUTIES,
  NOTIFICATION_EVENT_KINDS,
  NOTIFICATION_OPENED_VIA,
  NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS,
  NOTIFICATION_STATES,
  NOT_HELD_KINDS,
  ACCESS_PURPOSES,
  PRODUCED_KINDS,
  PRODUCTION_INSTRUMENTS,
  REPORT_HOLD_RELEASES,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import { closeDb, createDb, type Db } from "@korbat/db";
import { loadConfig } from "../../src/config";
import { pgError, rolledBack } from "./staff-fixtures";
import { recordCounts } from "./records-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 60_000 });

/**
 * The grants of the records to authorities (3f design, sections 6.5 and 6.7; invariant 12, the records). As korbat_api:
 * no privilege at all on authority_notifications, its events and productions, EXECUTE on seal_report and
 * report_close_unsealed refused, and only reports_owed() and erase_authority_records() callable. As korbat_auth: no
 * privilege on auth.report_holds, and EXECUTE on auth.address_held, auth.address_held_until and auth.address_hold_final
 * alone of 0030's functions, and on auth.address_hold_told of 3f's review (0032). Each closed list's CHECK is its contracts' constant, and the times are forced.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: the grants of the records to authorities", () => {
  let apiDb: Db;
  let authDb: Db;
  let migrateDb: Db;
  let before: Record<string, number>;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const config = loadConfig();
    apiDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 2 });
    authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 2 });
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 2 });
    before = await recordCounts(migrateDb);
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await Promise.all([closeDb(apiDb), closeDb(authDb), closeDb(migrateDb)]);
  });

  const privileges = async (role: string, table: string) =>
    (await migrateDb.execute<{ p: string }>(sql`
      select p from unnest(array['SELECT', 'INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE', 'TRUNCATE', 'REFERENCES', 'TRIGGER']) p
       where has_table_privilege(${role}, ${table}, p) order by p`)).map((r) => r.p);
  const columnPrivileges = async (role: string, schema: string, table: string) =>
    (await migrateDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`
      select count(*)::int as n from information_schema.columns c, unnest(array['SELECT', 'INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'REFERENCES']) p
       where c.table_schema = ${schema} and c.table_name = ${table} and has_column_privilege(${role}, ${`${schema}.${table}`}, c.column_name, p)`))[0]!.n;
  const mayExecute = async (role: string, fn: string) =>
    (await migrateDb.execute<{ ok: boolean }>(sql`select has_function_privilege(${role}, ${fn}, 'EXECUTE') as ok`))[0]!.ok;
  const checkValues = async (table: string, name: string) =>
    [...((await migrateDb.execute<{ d: string }>(sql`select pg_get_constraintdef(oid) as d from pg_constraint where conname = ${name} and conrelid = ${table}::regclass`))[0]!.d.matchAll(/'([a-z_0-9]+)'/g))].map((m) => m[1]!);

  const FUNCTIONS = [
    "public.report_open()",
    "public.report_close_unsealed(uuid)",
    "public.reports_owed()",
    "public.seal_report(uuid)",
    "public.erase_authority_records()",
    "public.authority_records_times()",
    "auth.address_held_until(uuid)",
    "auth.address_held(uuid)",
    "auth.address_hold_final(uuid)",
    // 3f's review (0032_orders_review): whether the person was told of every seal behind a held address.
    "auth.address_hold_told(uuid)",
  ];

  test("korbat_api holds nothing on the three record tables, column by column too, and reads no row of them", async () => {
    for (const table of ["public.authority_notifications", "public.authority_notification_events", "public.productions"]) {
      expect(await privileges("korbat_api", table)).toEqual([]);
      expect(await columnPrivileges("korbat_api", "public", table.slice("public.".length))).toBe(0);
    }
    expect((await pgError(apiDb.execute(sql`select count(*) from public.authority_notifications`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
    expect((await pgError(apiDb.execute(sql`select count(*) from public.productions`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
    expect((await pgError(apiDb.execute(sql`insert into public.authority_notification_events (notification_id, kind, at, how, not_to_person) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'note', now(), 'x', false)`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
  });

  test("korbat_api may call reports_owed() and erase_authority_records() alone of 0030's functions; seal_report and report_close_unsealed are refused", async () => {
    const callable = [];
    for (const fn of FUNCTIONS) if (await mayExecute("korbat_api", fn)) callable.push(fn);
    expect(callable).toEqual(["public.reports_owed()", "public.erase_authority_records()"]);
    expect((await pgError(apiDb.execute(sql`select * from public.seal_report(gen_random_uuid())`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
    expect((await pgError(apiDb.execute(sql`select public.report_close_unsealed(gen_random_uuid())`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
    // What it may call answers a case, a kind and a time, or a count, and nothing more.
    const owed = await apiDb.execute<Record<string, unknown>>(sql`select * from public.reports_owed() limit 1`);
    for (const row of owed) expect(Object.keys(row).sort()).toEqual(["case_id", "kind", "since"]);
  });

  test("korbat_auth holds nothing on auth.report_holds and may call the auth.address_* reads alone of 0030's functions, and 0032's fourth", async () => {
    expect(await privileges("korbat_auth", "auth.report_holds")).toEqual([]);
    expect(await columnPrivileges("korbat_auth", "auth", "report_holds")).toBe(0);
    expect((await pgError(authDb.execute(sql`select count(*) from auth.report_holds`)))?.code).toBe("42501");
    const callable = [];
    for (const fn of FUNCTIONS) if (await mayExecute("korbat_auth", fn)) callable.push(fn);
    expect(callable).toEqual(["auth.address_held_until(uuid)", "auth.address_held(uuid)", "auth.address_hold_final(uuid)", "auth.address_hold_told(uuid)"]);
    const [row] = await authDb.execute<{ until: string | null; held: boolean; final: boolean; told: boolean }>(
      sql`select auth.address_held_until(gen_random_uuid()) as until, auth.address_held(gen_random_uuid()) as held, auth.address_hold_final(gen_random_uuid()) as final,
                 auth.address_hold_told(gen_random_uuid()) as told`,
    );
    // An account with no seal behind it reads as told: the mail may say what it holds.
    expect({ ...row }).toEqual({ until: null, held: false, final: false, told: true });
    // And nothing of the public record tables.
    expect(await privileges("korbat_auth", "public.authority_notifications")).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("every closed list's CHECK is its contracts' constant", async () => {
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notifications", "authority_notifications_state")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_STATES]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notifications", "authority_notifications_duties")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_DUTIES]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notifications", "authority_notifications_sent_kinds")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notifications", "authority_notifications_answer")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_ANSWERS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notifications", "authority_notifications_opened_via")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_OPENED_VIA]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.authority_notification_events", "authority_notification_events_kind")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_EVENT_KINDS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.productions", "productions_instrument")).toEqual([...PRODUCTION_INSTRUMENTS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.productions", "productions_purposes")).toEqual([...ACCESS_PURPOSES]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.productions", "productions_asked")).toEqual([...NOTIFICATION_SENT_KINDS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.productions", "productions_produced")).toEqual([...PRODUCED_KINDS]);
    expect(await checkValues("public.productions", "productions_not_held")).toEqual([...NOT_HELD_KINDS]);
    expect(await checkValues("auth.report_holds", "report_holds_release_reason")).toEqual([...REPORT_HOLD_RELEASES]);
  });

  test("the times are forced: opened_at and an event's at are the transaction's, unless an imported row supplies one that is not after the clock", async () => {
    await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const past = "2024-01-02 03:04:05+00";
      const [plain] = await tx.execute<{ id: string; forced: boolean }>(
        sql`insert into public.authority_notifications (state, duties, case_id, account_id, opened_at, opened_via) values ('owed', '{voluntary}', gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), ${past}::timestamptz, 'cli')
            returning id, opened_at = now() as forced`,
      );
      expect(plain!.forced).toBe(true);
      const [imported] = await tx.execute<{ id: string; kept: boolean; stamped: boolean }>(
        sql`insert into public.authority_notifications (state, duties, case_id, account_id, opened_at, opened_via, imported_at) values ('owed', '{voluntary}', gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), ${past}::timestamptz, 'cli', ${past}::timestamptz)
            returning id, opened_at = ${past}::timestamptz as kept, imported_at = now() as stamped`,
      );
      expect({ kept: imported!.kept, stamped: imported!.stamped }).toEqual({ kept: true, stamped: true });

        sql`insert into public.authority_notifications (state, duties, case_id, account_id, opened_at, opened_via, imported_at) values ('owed', '{voluntary}', gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), now() + interval '1 day', 'cli', now())
            returning opened_at = now() as forced`,
      );
      expect(future!.forced).toBe(true);
      // An update keeps the forced time.
      const [moved] = await tx.execute<{ kept: boolean }>(sql`update public.authority_notifications set opened_at = now() where id = ${imported!.id}::uuid returning opened_at = ${past}::timestamptz as kept`);
      expect(moved!.kept).toBe(true);
      // An event's time: the record's import decides.
      const [ev] = await tx.execute<{ forced: boolean }>(
        sql`insert into public.authority_notification_events (notification_id, kind, at, how, not_to_person) values (${plain!.id}::uuid, 'request', ${past}::timestamptz, 'by letter', false) returning at = now() as forced`,
      );
      expect(ev!.forced).toBe(true);
      const [kept] = await tx.execute<{ kept: boolean }>(
        sql`insert into public.authority_notification_events (notification_id, kind, at, how, not_to_person) values (${imported!.id}::uuid, 'request', ${past}::timestamptz, 'by letter', false) returning at = ${past}::timestamptz as kept`,
      );
      expect(kept!.kept).toBe(true);
      const [production] = await tx.execute<{ forced: boolean }>(
        sql`insert into public.productions (instrument, produced, opened_at) values ('demand', '{handle}', ${past}::timestamptz) returning opened_at = now() as forced`,
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { AuditExportLine, AuditPage } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../../src/auth";
import { runStaffCommand } from "../../src/cli/staff";
import { canonicalText, chainHash } from "../../src/staff";
import { RECOVERY_TABLES, restoreForTest, rowCounts, snapshotForTest } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { MARKED, recoveryWorld, type ConsoleStaff, type RecoveryWorld } from "./recovery-harness";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 120_000 });

const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);

/**
 * The daily copy over HTTP (3f design, sections 6.6, 7.16, 8.7 and 10.5; invariant 29): the download of the audit log's
 * tail is a confirmed action, refused without the key, and with it writes one row, its confirmed audit row
 * audit_exported, and no mark; its lines carry the chain's members as stored, so each hash recomputes off the server with
 * the canonical text alone. The mark records the copy, with the plain audit row copy_marked, only when the place holds the
 * hash and the caller's own newest confirmed download released that place; a download cut short records nothing, and the
 * next starts at the same place. A download by someone who did not take the last copy alerts every staff account
 * (copy_taken). staff.js audit-export marks under the system actor. The page carries the reader's newest copied place and
 * each row's key, and lists what one key confirmed in a period. The file restores the database it found.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: the daily copy of the audit log's tail", () => {
  let w: RecoveryWorld;
  let keeper: ConsoleStaff;
  let other: ConsoleStaff;
  let found: string;
  let before: Record<string, number>;
  let head = 0;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    w = recoveryWorld();
    before = await rowCounts(w.apiDb, [...RECOVERY_TABLES]);
    found = await snapshotForTest(w.migrateDb);
    keeper = await w.staff("moderator");
    other = await w.staff("admin");
    await filler(250);
  }, 120_000);
  afterAll(async () => {
    await w.close();
  });

  /** Rows of the server's own, committed, so that a download spans a few hundred places. */
  async function filler(n: number): Promise<void> {
    await w.migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into public.audit_log (actor_id, action, metadata) select ${SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID}::uuid, 'filler', jsonb_build_object('n', n) from generate_series(1, ${n}::int) n`);
  }
  const page = async (s: ConsoleStaff, query = "") => {
    const res = await s.b.fetch(`/api/staff/audit${query}`);
    expect(res.status, await res.clone().text()).toBe(200);
    return AuditPage.parse(await res.json());
  };
  const newestPlace = async () => Number((await w.migrateDb.execute<{ seq: string }>(sql`select seq::text as seq from public.audit_head where id = 1`))[0]!.seq);
  /** The download of the places after `after` up to `through`, confirmed with the member's key unless `key` is false. */
  async function download(s: ConsoleStaff, after: number, through: number, key = true): Promise<Response> {
    const params = { after, through };
    const stepUp = key ? await w.confirmation(s, { action: "audit_exported", target: { type: "audit", id: String(through) }, params }) : undefined;
    return s.b.fetch("/api/staff/audit/export", { json: { ...params, ...(stepUp ? { stepUp } : {}) }, headers: MARKED });
  }
  const linesOf = (text: string) => text.split(LF).filter((line) => line !== "").map((line) => AuditExportLine.parse(JSON.parse(line)));
  const recomputes = (line: ReturnType<typeof linesOf>[number]) =>
    chainHash(
      line.prevHash,
      canonicalText({
        chainVersion: line.v,
        chainSeq: line.place,
        id: line.id,
        createdAt: new Date(line.at),
        actorId: line.actor,
        action: line.action,
        targetType: line.targetType,
        targetId: line.targetId,
        requestId: line.requestId,
        staffSession: line.staffSession,
        keyId: line.keyId,
        actionHash: line.actionHash,
        stepUpText: line.stepUp,
        metadataText: line.metadata,
      }),
    ) === line.hash;
  const marksOf = async (staffId: string) => (await w.migrateDb.execute<{ place: number }>(sql`select place::int from public.copy_marks where staff_id = ${staffId}::uuid order by id`)).map((r) => r.place);

  test("the download needs the key; with it, it writes its confirmed row audit_exported alone and no mark, and every line recomputes off the server", async () => {
    const first = await page(keeper);
    expect(first.copy).toEqual({ lastPlace: null });
    head = first.entries[0]!.seq;
    expect(await w.refusal(await download(keeper, 0, head, false))).toEqual([403, "staff_step_up_required"]);
    const res = await download(keeper, 0, head);
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.headers.get("content-type")).toBe("application/x-ndjson");
    expect(res.headers.get("cache-control")).toBe("private, no-store");
    expect(res.headers.get("content-disposition")).toBe(`attachment; filename="korbat-audit-1-${head}.jsonl"`);
    const lines = linesOf(await res.text());
    expect(lines.map((line) => line.place)).toEqual(Array.from({ length: head }, (_, i) => i + 1));
    expect(lines.every(recomputes)).toBe(true);
    for (const [i, line] of lines.entries()) if (i > 0) expect(line.prevHash).toBe(lines[i - 1]!.hash);
    // A line holds the row's metadata as stored: the page never shows it.
    expect(lines.some((line) => line.metadata.includes('"n": '))).toBe(true);
    const [exported] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ actor: string; target: string; params: unknown; stepped: boolean }>(
      sql`select actor_id::text as actor, target_id as target, metadata -> 'params' as params, step_up is not null as stepped from public.audit_log where action = 'audit_exported' order by chain_seq desc limit 1`,
    );
    expect(exported).toEqual({ actor: keeper.id, target: String(head), params: { after: 0, through: head }, stepped: true });
    expect(await marksOf(keeper.id)).toEqual([]);
    // A download that would end after the newest place is refused once the key has confirmed it.
    expect(await w.refusal(await download(keeper, head, (await newestPlace()) + 1000))).toEqual([422, "invalid_request"]);
  });

  test("the mark: refused for another hash, for a place the caller's newest confirmed download did not release, and for a caller who downloaded nothing; then the copy is recorded with copy_marked", async () => {
    // The keeper's newest confirmed download now releases places after `head` (the refused one above): download again.
    const res = await download(keeper, 0, head);
    const lines = linesOf(await res.text());
    const last = lines[lines.length - 1]!;
    const mark = (s: ConsoleStaff, body: unknown) => s.b.fetch("/api/staff/audit/export/mark", { json: body, headers: MARKED });
    expect(await w.refusal(await mark(keeper, { through: head, hash: "0".repeat(64) }))).toEqual([409, "copy_mismatch"]);
    expect(await w.refusal(await mark(keeper, { through: head - 1, hash: lines[lines.length - 2]!.hash }))).toEqual([409, "copy_mismatch"]);
    expect(await w.refusal(await mark(other, { through: head, hash: last.hash }))).toEqual([409, "copy_mismatch"]);
    expect(await marksOf(keeper.id)).toEqual([]);
    const marked = await mark(keeper, { through: head, hash: last.hash });
    expect(marked.status, await marked.clone().text()).toBe(204);
    expect(await marksOf(keeper.id)).toEqual([head]);
    const [row] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ actor: string; meta: unknown; stepped: boolean }>(
      sql`select actor_id::text as actor, metadata as meta, step_up is not null as stepped from public.audit_log where action = 'copy_marked' order by chain_seq desc limit 1`,
    );
    expect(row).toEqual({ actor: keeper.id, meta: { after: 0, through: head, rows: head }, stepped: false });
    expect((await page(keeper)).copy).toEqual({ lastPlace: head });
    expect((await page(other)).copy).toEqual({ lastPlace: null });
  });

  test("a download cut short at line 200 leaves its confirmed row and no mark, and the next download starts at the same place", async () => {
    await filler(250);
    const through = await newestPlace();
    const res = await download(keeper, head, through);
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    const reader = res.body!.getReader();
    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
    let text = "";
    while (text.split(LF).length <= 200) {
      const chunk = await reader.read();
      if (chunk.done) break;
      text += decoder.decode(chunk.value, { stream: true });
    }
    await reader.cancel();
    expect(text.split(LF).length).toBeGreaterThan(200);
    const [exported] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ params: unknown }>(sql`select metadata -> 'params' as params from public.audit_log where action = 'audit_exported' and actor_id = ${keeper.id}::uuid order by chain_seq desc limit 1`);
    expect(exported!.params).toEqual({ after: head, through });
    expect(await marksOf(keeper.id)).toEqual([head]);
    expect((await page(keeper)).copy).toEqual({ lastPlace: head });
  });

  test("a download by an account that did not take the last copy alerts every staff account (copy_taken); the last downloader's own does not", async () => {
    const since = new Date();
    const taken = async () =>
      w.migrateDb.execute<{ rows: number }>(sql`select (facts ->> 'rows')::int as rows from public.alert_outbox where kind = 'copy_taken' and created_at >= ${since.toISOString()}::timestamptz order by id`);
    const through = await newestPlace();
    expect((await download(other, 0, 10)).status).toBe(200);
    await w.moderation.settle();
    expect((await taken()).map((r) => r.rows)).toEqual([10]);
    expect((await download(keeper, head, through)).status).toBe(200);
    await w.moderation.settle();
    expect((await taken()).map((r) => r.rows)).toEqual([10]);
  });

  test("staff.js audit-export prints the lines and marks the copy under the system actor, which no staff member's newest copy is", async () => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    const notes: string[] = [];
    const code = await runStaffCommand(["audit-export", "--after", String(head)], { DATABASE_URL_API: w.config.DATABASE_URL_API }, { log: (line) => out.push(line), error: (line) => notes.push(line) });
    expect(code).toBe(0);
    const lines = out.map((line) => AuditExportLine.parse(JSON.parse(line)));
    expect(lines[0]!.place).toBe(head + 1);
    expect(lines.every(recomputes)).toBe(true);
    expect(notes).toEqual([`audit-export: places ${head + 1} to ${lines[lines.length - 1]!.place}, ${lines.length} rows.`]);
    expect(await marksOf(SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID)).toEqual([lines[lines.length - 1]!.place]);
    expect((await page(keeper)).copy).toEqual({ lastPlace: head });
    const [row] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ actor: string }>(sql`select actor_id::text as actor from public.audit_log where action = 'copy_marked' order by chain_seq desc limit 1`);
    expect(row!.actor).toBe(SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID);
    // From its own newest copy when no place is given: only the mark's own row is newer now.
    const again: string[] = [];
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["audit-export"], { DATABASE_URL_API: w.config.DATABASE_URL_API }, { log: (line) => again.push(line), error: () => undefined })).toBe(0);
    expect(again.map((line) => (JSON.parse(line) as { action: string }).action)).toEqual(["copy_marked"]);
  });

  test("3f's review: once the newest copy is staff.js audit-export's, a console download alerts every staff account, the keeper's own too: the system holds the copy, not the caller", async () => {
    const since = new Date();
    expect((await marksOf(SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID)).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect((await download(keeper, 0, 5)).status).toBe(200);
    await w.moderation.settle();
    const [row] = await w.migrateDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.alert_outbox where kind = 'copy_taken' and created_at >= ${since.toISOString()}::timestamptz`);
    expect(row!.n).toBe(1);
  });

  test("the page names each row's key, and lists what one key confirmed in a period", async () => {
    const all = await page(keeper);
    const confirmed = all.entries.find((entry) => entry.action === "audit_exported" && entry.actionHash !== null)!;
    expect(confirmed.keyId).not.toBeNull();
    expect(all.entries.filter((entry) => entry.actionHash === null).every((entry) => entry.keyId === null)).toBe(true);
    const byKey = await page(keeper, `?key=${confirmed.keyId}`);
    expect(byKey.entries.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(byKey.entries.every((entry) => entry.keyId === confirmed.keyId && entry.actionHash !== null)).toBe(true);
    const later = new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
    expect((await page(keeper, `?key=${confirmed.keyId}&from=${later}`)).entries).toEqual([]);
    const res = await keeper.b.fetch(`/api/staff/audit?from=${later}`);
    expect(res.status).toBe(400);
  });

  test("leaves the database as the file found it", async () => {
    await w.moderation.settle();
    await restoreForTest(w.migrateDb, found);
    expect(await rowCounts(w.apiDb, [...RECOVERY_TABLES])).toEqual(before);
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/lab/README.md` (whole file)

```markdown
# The contention lab of moderation decisions

`contention.lab.ts` measures what a decision's transaction costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 2 and 12),
against the test database with migration 0016. The design names no place for it; it lives here.

It is a database lab. It issues its statements itself, as SQL: a decision is the lock on its subject's profile row, its
row in `decisions` and its rows in `decision_actions`, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, the author's
deletion and the purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue; the purge's delete is the ordered
delete by owner (`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = $1 order by id for
update) returning id`). An intake is the moderation module's `recordIntake`. It uses no code of a later task.

Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the lab leaves no decision, and writes no audit row but one: the R4
removal that the redaction's rounds need committed (the last section) is a real, confirmed decision. The accounts it commits
(the large ones, written in bulk by the migrator, and the pair for the two-session rounds) are removed when it ends.

## Running it

From `apps/api`, with the scratch stack's data services up and the test database migrated:

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts

No suite includes it (its file ends in `.lab.ts`). It takes three to four minutes. Each measurement is one line of JSON
in `.data/lab-contention.jsonl` at the repository's root (or the file `LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent`: the share of
processor time, over all cores, that was not idle in the second and a half before the measurement.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, first run: a saturated machine

PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container on a Windows machine shared with other work. The machine was saturated
throughout: `busyPercent` read 94 to 99 before every measurement, most of it other projects' containers. These numbers
are upper bounds for this hardware; the second run below, on a quieter machine, is the one the design asks for.

### An account's seal (one session; one image on each post)

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 97% | 104 ms | 180 ms | 254 ms | 282 ms | 232 ms |
| 5,000 | 99% | 18 ms | 1,123 ms | 1,057 ms | 1,131 ms | 995 ms |

- The seal taken while deciding locks the account's image rows in id order, writes one row of `seal_posts` for each post
  and writes every image row once. At 5,000 image posts the decision and its seal take 1.1 s, 0.19% of the ten minutes a
  step-up challenge lives.
- The seal for good that follows writes every image row twice in one transaction: the answer ends the first seal (each
  row back to visible, 1.06 s at 5,000), and the new seal seals each again (1.13 s). Lifting it is a fourth write (1.0 s).
- No post row is locked by any of them.

### The purge of an account (one session)

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 99% | 436 ms | 2,228 ms | 5,000 | 2.7 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 98% | 390 ms | 1,862 ms | 0 | 2.3 s |
| 20,000 | no | 94% | 1,471 ms | 6,090 ms | 20,000 | 7.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 97% | 1,724 ms | 5,821 ms | 0 | 7.6 s |

- The keep trigger reads the freeze once for each row: about 0.3 to 0.45 ms a row under this load, whether the row is
  then kept or deleted. The research lab's figures under load were 2 to 4 s at 5,000 rows and 7 to 16 s at 20,000; these
  lie at their lower end.
- "Frozen" is an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material about the account: every row is kept, and the delete
  answers none.

### A decision against everything else (two sessions, 40 rounds a pair, each side first in half of them)

Three decisions (an interim withhold of a post; a final removal that closes the post's case; a seal on the author's
account's case followed in the same transaction by the answer that ends it) against six other transactions (a like of
the post; a follow of the author; the author's deletion of the post; the author's purge; a notice of child sexual abuse
material that names the post and its author's account; a report of the post under a rule). Each side holds its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back. `busyPercent` was 96.

| decision | against | both completed | deadlocks | lock timeouts | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| interim withhold | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 236 ms |
| interim withhold | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 116 ms |
| interim withhold | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 158 ms |
| interim withhold | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 232 ms |
| interim withhold | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 409 ms |
| interim withhold | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 318 ms |
| closing removal | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 183 ms |
| closing removal | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 145 ms |
| closing removal | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 194 ms |
| closing removal | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 171 ms |
| closing removal | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 207 ms |
| closing removal | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 231 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 254 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 210 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 233 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 419 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 264 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 206 ms |

- 720 rounds, no deadlock and no lock timeout. The purge met none here either: the deadlock the design expects of it is
  with an intake that locks the account's image rows, which the intake does not do before Task 3.
- What makes this hold: a decision takes its subject's profile row first, as the author's deletion and the purge do; a
  like and a follow take that row in a mode a decision's does not conflict with; a seal locks image rows only; and an
  intake takes its cases in one order and each post's row only to read it.
- A finding the lab led to, now a test (`moderation-races.test.ts`): a report that arrives while a decision is closing
  its target's case waits where it opens a case (`insert into cases ... on conflict do nothing` waits for the transaction
  that is changing the conflicting row), and then opens a new case without a retry. The retry on `case_closed` is needed
  only when the decision has locked the case and not yet closed it when the report reads it.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, second run: the final migration, a quieter machine

Run again after the review added a second deferred check to 0016 (queued by every row of the ledger, it runs at COMMIT,
which the lab's rolled-back transactions never reach). `busyPercent` read 17 to 28.

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 19% | 35 ms | 70 ms | 115 ms | 110 ms | 107 ms |
| 5,000 | 17% | 7 ms | 420 ms | 463 ms | 503 ms | 465 ms |

At 5,000 image posts the seal taken while deciding takes 0.43 s with its decision, 0.07% of the challenge's ten minutes;
the seal for good that follows it writes every image row twice in under a second.

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 28% | 182 ms | 888 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 24% | 108 ms | 791 ms | 0 | 0.9 s |
| 20,000 | no | 22% | 680 ms | 2,488 ms | 20,000 | 3.2 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 27% | 576 ms | 2,366 ms | 0 | 2.9 s |

The keep trigger costs about 0.12 to 0.18 ms a row here.

The two-session rounds at 24% busy: the same 18 pairs of 40 rounds each, every transaction completed, no deadlock and no
lock timeout, the longest transaction 124 ms.

# The lab of the intake's lock statement

`hold.lab.ts` measures what an intake's hold costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 5 and 12, Task 3), at the
repository: `MediaForCases.hold` with an owner pair, which is the statement that locks every image row on an account's
posts when a report of child sexual abuse material names the account
(`select ... from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id where m.post_id = any($1) or m.owner_id = any($2) order
by m.id for key share of m`). It also times the disposal's two statements over the same accounts, and runs the purge
against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post. It runs against the test database with migration 0016,
through the media repository and the moderation module's own `recordIntake`; the purge is the social repository's
`purgeProfile` with the media repository's `purgeOwner` as its last act. Every measured transaction is rolled back; the
accounts it commits are removed when it ends.

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts test/lab/hold.lab.ts

It takes about a minute and a quarter. Each measurement is one line of JSON in `.data/lab-hold.jsonl` (or the file
`LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent` as above. `LAB_ROUNDS` sets how many rounds the two sessions meet by chance (40
unless said).

## The numbers of 2026-10-04

Three runs on the shared Windows machine, PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container: two before the review of
Task 3 and one after its fixes. The machine was never quiet, most of the load other projects' containers:
`busyPercent` read 14 to 40 before the lock statement's runs of the first run (up to 100 before its last measurements),
14 to 83 before those of the second and 15 to 40 throughout the third. The times are upper bounds.

### The lock statement (`hold` with one owner pair; one image on each post; three runs each, a transaction of its own each)

| attached rows | run | busy | lock statement | WAL written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | first | 29 to 40% | 36, 25 and 21 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | second | 64 to 83% | 90, 65 and 26 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 46, 31 and 28 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 20,000 | first | 14 to 19% | 114, 80 and 69 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | second | 14 to 76% | 102, 180 and 198 ms | 1,408, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 151, 123 and 102 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |

- The research lab's figures (`lab-gate-k`, H) were 77 ms and 287 kB at 5,000 rows and 102 ms and 1.1 MB at 20,000:
  these agree. The lock writes its mark to each row it takes, though no column changes: about 55 bytes of WAL a row.
- The plan is LockRows over a Sort on `m.id` over a hash join of `post_media` and `posts`, as the design says of the
  owner form. In the test database the lab's account owns most image rows, so `post_media` is scanned whole; the sort
  took 0.6 MB of memory at 5,000 rows and 2.5 MB at 20,000.
- A whole notice on the path for child sexual abuse material that names the account (its rows, the copy of the profile,
  the hold and the snapshot) took 72, 95 and 77 ms at 5,000 rows and 104, 238 and 147 ms at 20,000; one that names a
  post of the account as well took 85, 91 and 80 ms at 5,000 and 743 (at 90% busy), 299 and 147 ms at 20,000.
- The purge's ordered delete (`purgeOwner`) right after such a notice, in the same transaction, deleted no row: 1.4,
  1.6 and 1.3 s at 5,000 rows, 5.6 and 5.5 s (73 to 100% busy) and 3.2 s (31% busy) at 20,000, the keep trigger reading
  the freeze once for each row.

### The disposal's two statements (one batch of `dropDisposable`, and `overdueDeletions`)

The account's rows are all attached. In the first two lines nothing of the account is disposable: its posts are
visible. In the last, the account is reported on the path for child sexual abuse material and every post of it is
deleted, so every row carries a mark of disposal and none may go.

| what | attached rows | busy | `dropDisposable` | `overdueDeletions` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing disposable, the freeze a condition of its own (as first built) | 5,000 | 100% | 3,332 ms | 3,332 ms |
| | 20,000 | 97% | 14,226 ms | 13,863 ms |
| nothing disposable, the marks tested first (as built now) | 5,000 | 24% | 18 ms | 8 ms |
| | 20,000 | 40% | 62 ms | 19 ms |
| every row marked and frozen (as built now) | 5,000 | 18% | 1,285 ms | 1,174 ms |
| | 20,000 | 26% | 4,148 ms | 3,666 ms |

- As first built, the predicate was `... and (marks) and (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))`.
  The second condition names `post_media` alone, so the planner made it the filter of that table's scan and called the
  freeze for every attached image row in the table before a mark was tested. The review measured 0.9 s at 5,000 rows
  and 3.4 s at 20,000 on a quieter machine; the first two lines are the same statement on a saturated one.
- Now the marks and the freeze are one condition, `case when (marks) then (m.post_id is null or not
  public.post_frozen(m.post_id)) else false end`: it names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined, and the
  freeze is read only for a row that carries a mark. `media-cases.test.ts` pins that no scan's filter names the
  predicate, under the planner's own plan and under each join method alone.
- What remains is the last pair of lines: a frozen account whose posts are all deleted (a purged account under an
  unanswered report, or under a seal for good) costs one read of the freeze for each kept row, about 0.2 ms, at every
  round of the disposal and at every count of overdue rows, for as long as the freeze lasts.

### The purge against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post

A report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is taken in as two items, so a notice about a
post that quotes its author's own post holds two posts of one account for share, in id order, while the purge writes
both. The lab's account has such a pair, four images on each post; the notice names the quoting post and the account.
The notice's side counts the runs the moderation module made, so a deadlock it absorbed by running again shows; nothing
runs a purge again, so a deadlock that picks the purge shows as its error.

By chance (two sessions, each side first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead, each holding its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back):

| purge | rounds | busy | purge | notice | deadlocks | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as first built (counters, then the posts in id order) | 200 | 95% | 200 of 200 | 200 of 200, each in one run | 0 | 528 ms |
| as built now (every post locked first, in id order) | 40 | 25% | 40 of 40 | 40 of 40, each in one run | 0 | 139 ms |

Staged (ten rounds a shape: the notice has copied the first of the two posts and is held there, the purge comes to
wait, the notice goes on to the second post):

| purge | the quoting post has the lower id | the quoted post has the lower id and was deleted by its author |
|---|---|---|
| as first built: the counters of what its posts quote, then the posts in id order | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 | not run |
| the account's posts that are not deleted locked first, in id order | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 |
| every post of the account locked first, in id order (as built now) | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: both complete |

- As first built, the purge's quote counter wrote the quoted post before the ordered statement asked for the quoting
  one, which the notice held: each waited for the other. The window is one statement of the notice wide, so 200 rounds
  by chance never met it, and every staged round did. PostgreSQL ended the purge each time: a session looks for a
  deadlock once it has waited a second, and the purge was the first to wait. The notice went through in one run. A purge
  that ends this way is finished by the purge job within five minutes.
- Locking only the posts that are not deleted leaves the same wait in the second shape: a live post that quotes (or
  replies to) its author's own deleted post has that post's counter written by the purge, and a report of child sexual
  abuse material holds a deleted post like any other. So the purge locks every post of the account first.
- What stays unordered: the counters of other accounts' posts that the purged account replied to, quoted, liked or
  reposted, which the purge writes after its own posts; and the author's deletion of one post, which writes the post
  and then the post it replied to or quoted.
- Before the review this pair ran with two plain posts (and with the purge as first built): 40 of 40 on both sides in
  both runs, no deadlock, the longest transaction 307 ms at 64% busy and 200 ms at 23%.
- What the two-session tests add (`media-cases.test.ts`): when the notice locks first, the purge waits and then keeps
  every attached row; when the purge deletes first, the notice waits, locks nothing and is stored without an error.

### The contention lab again

`contention.lab.ts` issues the purge's statements as the repositories issue them since Task 3: every post of the
account locked in id order (`select id from posts where author_id = $1 order by id for update`), then the tombstones,
and the ordered delete of the image rows last. Three runs on 2026-10-04 with the intake locking image rows and placing
its holds. The first, before the review, still tombstoned by one ordered statement and met a machine at 9 to 14% busy
(53 and 93 before the two purges of 20,000 rows). The second and the third issue the statements above: the second met
a saturated machine (93 to 100% throughout), so its times say more about the machine than about the change; the third
a quiet one (6 to 16%). "Tombstones" is the lock statement and the update together.

| image rows | frozen | run | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | first | 9% | 170 ms | 891 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | first | 14% | 120 ms | 827 ms | 0 | 1.0 s |
| 20,000 | no | first | 53% | 603 ms | 4,019 ms | 20,000 | 4.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | first | 93% | 1,440 ms | 4,249 ms | 0 | 5.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | second | 100% | 481 ms | 3,136 ms | 5,000 | 3.6 s |
| 5,000 | yes | second | 100% | 309 ms | 3,423 ms | 0 | 3.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | second | 100% | 1,934 ms | 8,112 ms | 20,000 | 10.1 s |
| 20,000 | yes | second | 100% | 2,249 ms | 8,467 ms | 0 | 10.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | third | 16% | 91 ms | 827 ms | 5,000 | 0.9 s |
| 5,000 | yes | third | 6% | 103 ms | 730 ms | 0 | 0.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | third | 13% | 442 ms | 2,207 ms | 20,000 | 2.7 s |
| 20,000 | yes | third | 13% | 481 ms | 1,977 ms | 0 | 2.5 s |

Locking the posts first costs nothing that shows: at 5,000 posts the lock statement and the update together took 91
and 103 ms, where the one ordered statement took 170 and 120 ms.

The 18 pairs of 40 rounds: in every run each transaction completed, with no deadlock and no lock timeout; the longest
transaction was 137 ms in the first (12% busy), 562 ms in the second (100% busy) and 116 ms in the third (13% busy).
The account's seal taken while deciding: 84 ms at 1,000 image posts and 2.2 s at 5,000 in the first run (13% busy; 0.4
and 1.1 s in Task 2's runs), 361 ms and 3.3 s in the second, 58 and 156 ms in the third.

### What the lab's tests found

- **A batch that was not one.** `dropDisposable` as the design writes it (`delete from post_media where id in (select
  ... order by id limit $1 for update)`) can delete more than its limit. When the planner joins the delete's rows to
  the sub-select by a nested loop, the sub-select runs again for every row; each run skips the rows this statement has
  deleted already and lets the next ones in. On a fresh test database one call deleted all 60 disposable rows under a
  limit of 25, and with hash joins, merge joins, materialising, hashed aggregation and sorting switched off it deleted
  33 of 36. The repository therefore chooses the batch in a materialized common table expression, which runs once
  whatever the plan (`with batch as materialized (select ... order by m.id limit $1 for update of m) delete from
  post_media where id in (select id from batch) returning id`); `media-cases.test.ts` holds the bound under those
  planner settings. The ordered deletes of the author's deletion and the purge have no limit, so the same re-run changes
  nothing they delete.
- **The freeze read for every row.** The disposal's two statements, above.
- **The purge and its own posts.** The staged rounds, above.

## The numbers of 2026-10-09: the R4 redaction (migration 0018)

`contention.lab.ts` gains one test for `redact_r4_body` (3c design, sections 2 and 6.4): the redaction takes its
decision's case, then the post, then the post's images in id order, the order of `moderation_apply` and of an intake's
locks, and the design asks for it to be measured against both. The post has four images. Its R4 removal is the one
thing this lab confirms with a real staff key (the software authenticator, as `decideForTest` does), because a
redaction acts only on a committed decision; it is dated back seven months, so that it is final for its author. The
redaction itself, and everything that runs against it, is rolled back in every round, so each round finds the decision
due again. The removal's case goes with the lab's accounts at the end; its one audit row stays, as every real
decision's does. Run alone with `-t "the R4 redaction"`.

Two runs: the test alone on a machine busy with other work (`busyPercent` 82), then the whole file on a quieter one
(`busyPercent` 22; the whole file took 122 s).

| the redaction against | rounds | redaction | other side | longest transaction, busy | longest, quieter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (alone, one session) | 1 | ok | | 67 ms | 29 ms |
| an interim withhold on the post's other, open case, whose trigger runs `moderation_apply` on the post | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 233 ms | 68 ms |
| a report under a rule, which locks the post `FOR SHARE` and holds its images | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 125 ms | 104 ms |
| a notice of child sexual abuse material naming the post and its author's account, which locks the images through both | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 123 ms | 83 ms |

- No deadlock and no refusal in 120 rounds of either run, each side first in half of them. The redaction and a decision on the post's
  other case meet at the post's row, which both take `FOR UPDATE` before any image row; the redaction and a report meet
  there too (`FOR UPDATE` against `FOR SHARE`); a notice that reaches the images through the account takes them
  `FOR KEY SHARE`, which the redaction's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not wait for.
- That last pair is the one the design accepts as a race and not as a wait (6.4): a report about the author's account
  that commits between the redaction's check of the freeze and its erasure of the snapshots leaves the body blank, the
  snapshots kept and the decision unmarked, and the round after the answer finishes it. The database test of
  `redact_r4_body` stages exactly that.
```
