/**
 * The moderation codes the console can meet (3c design, sections 8 and 10): those of the case routes, of a decision, of
 * a review, of a finding's link and of a reveal. The codes of the app's own report form, appeal and re-examination never
 * reach the console.
 */
export const CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES = [
  "notice_link_invalid",
  "notice_link_offsite",
  "case_changed",
  "case_closed",
  "staff_recused",
  "staff_target",
  "admin_required",
  "reviewer_conflict",
  "decision_cap",
  "profile_changed",
  "snapshot_mismatch",
  "snapshot_erased",
  "text_invalid",
  "text_quotes_user",
  "text_not_found",
  "invalid_decision",
  "image_refused",
  "reveal_refused",
  // 3e (design, section 8.9): the first three are the ones the composer meets; the other two cannot reach the console
  // today and are worded so that the table has an entry for each code of the type.
  "strike_mismatch",
  "standing_conflict",
  "ground_not_established",
  "reply_not_open",
  "reporting_restricted",
  // 3f (design, section 8.9): a message at the contact point that someone else closed meanwhile; and the refusals of
  // Task 2's order routes.
  "message_handled",
  "order_needs_message",
  "order_exists",
  "order_closed",
  "order_event_refused",
  "already_released",
  // 3f Task 3 (design, sections 8.5 and 8.9): the refusals of giving effect to an order.
  "order_changed",
  "order_not_verified",
  "order_cap",
  // 3f Task 6 (design, sections 8.7 to 8.9): a gap that is closed or that a decision does not fit, and a copy mark the
  // database did not take.
  "gap_mismatch",
  "copy_mismatch",
] as const satisfies readonly ModerationErrorCode[];
export type ConsoleModerationCode = (typeof CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES)[number];

/** 3f Task 6 [copy.broken] (8.7): a download that broke off, whose mark the database refused or the console never sent. */
const COPY_BROKEN = "The download broke off, or its lines do not continue each other. Nothing was recorded as copied: press again.";

/** 3f [open.duplicate]: an order of this state, authority and reference is recorded already (order_exists). */
const OPEN_DUPLICATE =
  "An order of this authority with this reference is already recorded. If that record is wrong, correct it on its screen; if it is closed, an admin reopens it there. Do not open the order a second time under a changed reference.";

/** The console's words for each of them. A recusal reads the same whether the conflict concerns the author or a reporter. */
export const MODERATION_MESSAGES: Record<ConsoleModerationCode, string> = {
  notice_link_invalid: "That link does not name a post or a profile on korbat.",
  notice_link_offsite: "That link leads to another site. A case is opened only on a post or a profile of this korbat.",

  staff_target: "A final decision cannot restrict a staff account: staff are disciplined by demotion. A measure taken while deciding can.",
  admin_required: "Only an admin can take this decision.",
  reviewer_conflict: "You cannot review this appeal: you made a decision in its case, or opened a finding in it. Another staff member must review it.",
  decision_cap: "You have reached the limit on decisions one staff account may confirm for now. Try again later.",

  standing_conflict: STANDING_CONFLICT,
  ground_not_established: STANDING_TERMINATE_R2,
  reply_not_open: "This measure takes no reply: it has ended or was lifted.",
  reporting_restricted: "That account's reports under the rules are restricted.",

  // [effect.cap] (8.5 block 4).
  order_cap: `You have given effect to ${ORDER_RULES.decisionsPerDay} order items in 24 hours, the most one staff account may. Another staff member goes on; tell the operator at once.`,
  gap_mismatch: "That gap is closed already, or this decision does not take again what it lost. Read After a restore again.",

/** A small number as a word, as the design's sentences write it; a larger one in digits. */
const inWords = (n: number): string => ["zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve"][n] ?? String(n);

/** A removal order's hour (ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes) in the words the console's sentences use. */
const HOUR_WORDS = ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes === 60 ? "one hour" : `${ORDER_RULES.hourMinutes} minutes`;
/** The last choice of the form "Open an order" (Task 2), which every sentence that sends a person there names. */
const NOT_LISTED = '"The message is not listed"';

 * 3f (design, sections 8.2, 8.3 and 18): the console's sentences of authorities' orders, each under the design's key

 * every time is the database's instant, printed by bothTimes. Later tasks of 3f add their keys here.

 * every time is the database's instant, printed by the screen with bothTimes.

  // The audit log's download (8.7).

  key: "The file holds more than this page: confirm with your staff key.",
  downloadButton: "Download since my last copy",
  done: (from: number, to: number, rows: number) => `Downloaded places ${from} to ${to}: ${rows} rows. The copy is recorded.`,
  none: (lastPlace: number) => `Nothing is newer than place ${lastPlace}.`,
  broken: COPY_BROKEN,
  // "What one key confirmed" (8.7).
  keyTitle: "What one key confirmed",
  keyWhat:
    "Use this when a key may have been in someone else's hands. Each decision listed is undone by an admin's correction on its case; there is no batch. An order's disabling is reinstated only on one of its grounds: a stolen key is not one, so check the order itself.",
  keyField: "Staff key's id",
  keyFrom: "From (UTC, for example 2026-10-10T01:00:00Z)",
  keyTo: "To (UTC)",
  keyShow: "Show what it confirmed",
  keyAll: "All rows",
  keyRule: "Enter a key's id as staff.js keys prints it, and each time as 2026-10-10T01:00:00Z, or leave a time empty.",
  thisKey: "This key",
  keyShown: (keyId: string) => `Rows a step-up of the key ${keyId} confirmed, newest first.`,
  // Home (8.2).
  homeCopy: (days: number) => `The copy is ${days} ${days === 1 ? "day" : "days"} old. The keeper downloads the audit log's tail on the daily visit: Audit log, "Download since my last copy".`,
  /** [home.copy] before any copy was taken: the design's sentence has no age to print then. */
  homeCopyNone: `No copy of the audit log's tail has been taken yet. The keeper downloads it on the daily visit: Audit log, "Download since my last copy".`,
  homeRestore: (open: number, measures: number) =>
    `After a restore: ${open} ${open === 1 ? "gap is" : "gaps are"} open, ${measures} of them measures to take again. Keep the app's site closed (APP_SITE=closed, Caddy recreated) until every order disabling and seal among them is back.`,
  // After a restore (8.8).
  title: "After a restore",
  what: "The database was restored from a backup, and the keeper's copy names what the backup lacks. Nothing below is in force until a person takes it again under a key: korbat imports no measure. Work from the top.",
  // 3f's review (operations1): the operator's step closes the site, which korbat cannot see; the screen says what to keep.
  site: "Keep the app's site closed (APP_SITE=closed, Caddy recreated) until no order disabling and no seal is open here.",
  siteOpen: "No order disabling and no seal is open. The operator may open the app's site (APP_SITE=open, Caddy recreated).",
  retention: "No measure is open. The operator may switch retention and the image sweep back on.",
  lost: "What no import brings back: the texts of the lost decisions, everything after the keeper's last download, and anything the keeper's files do not hold (the import printed every place it found missing in them). For those, the contact-point mailbox and the operator's notes are the record.",
  holds:
    "Before you disable anything again for an order: whoever has the server compares each held notice below with the contact-point mailbox since the keeper's last download. An extension or a later time that was recorded after that download is lost, and a disabling taken again under the old end would tell the author early.",
  holdUntil: (until: string | null) => (until === null ? "Held with no end recorded" : `Held until ${until}`),
  importedAt: (at: string) => `The newest import ran at ${at}.`,
  nothingOpen: "Every gap is closed.",
  classes: {
    order_effect: { heading: "Orders: disable again", line: (n: number, actedAt: string) => `Lost: the disabling of ${n} ${n === 1 ? "post" : "posts"} for an order, first done at ${actedAt}.` },
    seal_final: { heading: "Seals for good", line: (actedAt: string) => `Lost: a seal for good, decided at ${actedAt}.` },
    seal_interim: { heading: "Seals taken while deciding", line: (actedAt: string) => `Lost: a seal taken while deciding, decided at ${actedAt}.` },
    standing: { heading: "Suspensions and terminations", line: (measure: string, actedAt: string) => `Lost: ${measure}, decided at ${actedAt}.` },
    restriction: { heading: "Other restrictions", line: (measure: string, actedAt: string) => `Lost: ${measure}, decided at ${actedAt}.` },
    reversal: { heading: "Reversals", line: (actedAt: string) => `Lost: a reversal, decided at ${actedAt}.` },

    },
  },
  /** {what} of a gap of the class record: the words of its lost row's action. */
  recordWhat: (action: string) =>
    action === "notification_recorded"

  orderLine: "Open the order, then Disable for an order: the preservation's end, the hold and the clock keep their imported values. Read the held notices above first.",
  openOrder: "Open the order",

  notNeededDone: "Closed as not needed.",
  closed: (disposition: "reapplied" | "not_needed" | "imported", at: string) =>
    `${disposition === "reapplied" ? "Taken again" : disposition === "not_needed" ? "Not needed" : "Entered again"} at ${at}.`,
  /** [restore.again] (8.8): the composer's line when a decision takes a lost one again. */
  again: (actedAt: string) => `This takes again a decision of ${actedAt} that was lost with a restore. Its statement says so. Write the facts and the reason again: the lost texts are gone.`,

  effectPreserveAgain: (preserveUntil: string) => `Each post, its images and a copy of its text are preserved until ${preserveUntil}, as before the restore.`,
} as const;

  dismissed: "Answered a report of child sexual abuse material without a seal",
};

/** The two kinds of decision the composer offers, as it names them. */
export const COMPOSER_KINDS: Record<"interim" | "final", string> = {
  interim: "While deciding",
  final: "Decide the case",
};

/** The three outcomes the composer offers, as it names them. */
export const COMPOSER_OUTCOMES: Record<"restricted" | "no_violation" | "not_evident", string> = {
  restricted: "Restrict",
  no_violation: "No breach",
  not_evident: "Illegality not evident",
};

/**
 * The composer's sentences beside its texts and its preview. The rule on personal data is the design's sentence in three
 * parts, so that each part is written once: the rule itself, and where the text goes, which differs for a decision
 * without a measure: its author never receives its texts, whether the decision is told to them (it ended what korbat did
 * while deciding) or to nobody. The other three say what the preview cannot show yet, or will not.
 */
export const COMPOSER_WORDS = {
  personalDataRule: 'Write only about the author\'s content and conduct. Never copy another person\'s name, handle, address or other personal data here: describe it (for example "the home address of another person").',
  toAuthor: "The author receives this text by email and keeps it while their account exists.",
  staysInRecord: "The author never receives this text: a decision without a measure tells them at most that what korbat did while deciding has ended. It stays in the case's record, for staff.",
  noStatement: "No statement is sent: this decision restricts nothing and ends nothing that was done while deciding.",
  previewAfterSnapshot: "The preview follows the fresh snapshot: the case's newest snapshot cannot be shown, so Confirm takes a fresh one, shows it, and asks you to confirm again.",
  sealSettled: "The numbers, the sentence about posts their author had deleted, and whether the seal changes anything are settled when the seal is recorded: the statement its author gets holds them as they are then.",
} as const;

/**
 * The shared codes a staff route may also answer, and the console's own: a network failure, an answer its schemas refuse,
 * a browser prompt that did not finish, step-up options that bind something other than the action the person chose, and
 * sign-in or enrolment options whose challenge is not one of that ceremony's.
 */
const OTHER_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  challenge_expired: "That took too long. Try again.",
  rate_limited: "Too many attempts. Wait a while, then try again.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  not_found: "That no longer exists.",
  csrf_failed: "This request could not be verified. Reload the page and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
  internal: "Something went wrong on the server. Try again.",
  network: "The staff console's server cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.",
  invalid_answer: "The server's answer could not be read. Reload the page and try again.",
  ceremony_cancelled: "Nothing was signed: the browser's prompt was closed or timed out. Try again.",
  key_already_registered: "This key is already registered for your staff account. Use another key.",
  ceremony_refused: "The browser refused to use a key here. Open the console at exactly the address in CONSOLE_ORIGIN, never at 127.0.0.1, and try again.",
  step_up_mismatch:
    "The confirmation could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than this action, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  signin_mismatch:
    "The sign-in could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than a sign-in, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  enroll_mismatch:
    "The registration could not be checked: the server asked your key for something other than a staff key's registration, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
};

const FALLBACK = "Something went wrong. Try again.";

/** The console's words for a code; a code it does not know, a passkey code included, gets the plain fallback. */
export function messageFor(code: string): string {
  if (Object.hasOwn(STAFF_MESSAGES, code)) return STAFF_MESSAGES[code as StaffErrorCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(MODERATION_MESSAGES, code)) return MODERATION_MESSAGES[code as ConsoleModerationCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(OTHER_MESSAGES, code)) return OTHER_MESSAGES[code]!;
  return FALLBACK;
}

/** The code of anything a screen's action threw, or null: the console's errors carry one. */
export function codeOf(err: unknown): string | null {
  return err instanceof Error && "code" in err && typeof err.code === "string" ? err.code : null;
}

/**
 * The words for anything a screen's action threw: the console's errors carry a code, anything else is the fallback.
 * `words` gives a screen's own words for a code where the shared ones would say too little: which daily limit was
 * reached, or what a link that names nothing means on the form it was typed into.
 */
export function describeError(err: unknown, words: Record<string, string> = {}): string {
  const code = codeOf(err);
  if (code === null) return FALLBACK;
  return Object.hasOwn(words, code) ? words[code]! : messageFor(code);
}

import type { DeleteConfirmRequest, DeleteStartResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AuthError, type AuthDeps, type RequestContext } from "../context";
import { randomToken } from "../crypto";
import { HOUR, enforceLimit } from "../limits";
import type { Session } from "../sessions";
import { CODE_TTL_MS, checkEmailCode, emailCodeHash, flowKey, newEmailCode, sendCode } from "./email";
import { noticeTime, notifyAccount } from "./notify";

export const DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR = 3;

/** The deletion a code is out for: kept under the hashed flow id until the code is entered or expires. */
export interface PendingDeletion {
  userId: string;
}

/**
 * Mails the deletion code to the account's own address (1b design, section 7.6): the second of the
 * three guards, after the fresh session the route demands and before the handle the owner types. The
 * code row carries the owner, so no other account can spend it.
 */
export async function startDeletion(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<DeleteStartResponse> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `delete-start:${user.id}`, DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR, HOUR);
  const flowId = randomToken();
  const code = newEmailCode();
  await deps.repo.createEmailCode({
    flowId,
    email: user.email,
    userId: user.id,
    purpose: "delete_account",
    codeHash: emailCodeHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, flowId, code),
    expiresAt: new Date(deps.now().getTime() + CODE_TTL_MS),
    ipHash: ctx.ipHash,
  });
  const pending: PendingDeletion = { userId: user.id };
  await deps.kv.set(flowKey(flowId), JSON.stringify(pending), CODE_TTL_MS);
  await sendCode(deps, { to: user.email, template: "delete_account_code", data: { code } });
  return { flowId };
}

/**
 * Writes the cache tombstones of sessions the database has just revoked, so a cached copy cannot serve
 * them for the rest of its minute. Best effort: the rows are revoked whatever happens here, so a failure
 * only lets a cached copy live out that minute, and the account is not left half gone because the cache
 * was unreachable.
 */
async function tombstoneQuietly(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, sessionIds: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.sessions.tombstone(sessionIds);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, userId }, "account deletion: the session tombstones could not be written; the sessions are revoked in the database");
  }
}

/**
 * The auth side of a deletion, step 1 of section 7.6: the typed handle must be the account's own,
 * then the code must be right; then, in one transaction, the account is marked deleted (every lookup
 * treats the row as absent from here, so no request can succeed against it while the purge runs),
 * every session revoked, its devices, codes and passkeys deleted, its WebAuthn user handle cleared and
 * the event recorded; then the revoked sessions get their tombstones, so the cache cannot revive one,
 * and the account is told. Nothing after the transaction can fail the request: the account is gone
 * once it commits. The row itself is anonymised by finishPurge, once the account module has purged the
 * other schemas.
 */
export async function confirmDeletion(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, input: DeleteConfirmRequest): Promise<void> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  // The handle is the third guard, compared in any case and checked before the code, so a slip of the fingers costs no attempt on it.
  const profile = await deps.profiles.find(user.id);
  if (!profile || profile.handle.toLowerCase() !== input.handle.toLowerCase()) throw new AuthError("invalid_request", 400, "handle_mismatch");
  const row = await deps.repo.findEmailCode(input.flowId);
  // A code from another account's deletion, or from any other flow, is no code at all, settled before an attempt is counted.
  if (row?.purpose !== "delete_account" || row.userId !== user.id) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  await checkEmailCode(deps, row, input.flowId, input.code);
  // Taken, not read: whatever happens next, this flow is over and the code is spent.
  if (!(await deps.kv.take(flowKey(input.flowId)))) throw new AuthError("code_expired", 400);

  const revoked = await deps.repo.takeDown(user.id, deps.now(), session.deviceId);
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, user.id, revoked);
  // Told once the account is gone, and never before: a take-down that failed leaves the account as it was. The address
  // still belongs to the row until finishPurge; best effort, since no mail failure may keep an account its owner has given up.
  // 3f (W.5): one wording for every account, and the hold's paragraph when its address is held for a report.
  await notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "account_deleted", await heldAddressFacts(deps, user.id));
}

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 7.15 and W.5): what a deletion's mail says of an address held for a report to the authorities:
 * the day the hold ends at the latest (heldUntil, a UTC day, from auth.address_held_until) and which of the paragraph's
 * two variants (holdFinal, from auth.address_hold_final: a seal for good, or one taken while deciding). Nothing while
 * REPORT_HOLD is off or nothing is held. Best effort, as the mail is: a failed read is logged and the mail goes in its one
 * wording for every account, which says that korbat keeps what the law obliges it to keep for a time.
 *
 * 3f's review (access3): nothing either while a seal that holds the address is held with an order's notice (`told`
 * false): the paragraph says that korbat sealed images of the account, which the person has not been told. The address
 * stays held all the same; the mail goes in the one wording for every account.
 */
async function heldAddressFacts(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  if (!deps.config.reportHold) return {};
  try {
    const hold = await deps.repo.addressHold(userId);
    return hold === null || !hold.told ? {} : { heldUntil: hold.until.toISOString().slice(0, 10), holdFinal: String(hold.final) };
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err }, "account deletion: whether the address is held could not be read; the mail goes without the hold's paragraph");
    return {};
  }
}

/**
 * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.8 step 3): the take-down of an account whose termination is final for its author, as the
 * system, without a session or a code. As confirmDeletion does: the account's row is read first with its address, then
 * the account is marked deleted with every session revoked and the event written, in one transaction; the revoked
 * sessions get their tombstones; and only after that commit the address read before gets termination_final, best
 * effort, in place of account_deleted, with the decision's day and, when images of the account stay sealed, its
 * sentence about them. It does nothing a second time: an account already marked deleted (gone from every lookup) is
 * left as it is, with no event and no mail, and the answer is false; true only for the take-down this call made. The
 * address stays on the row until finishPurge, so nothing is lost by mailing after the commit.
 *
 * The mail is started and not waited for (3e's review, database3): the moderation module's take-down calls this while its
 * own transaction holds the account's profile FOR UPDATE, and a relay that stalls would hold that row, and every like,
 * repost and reply of the account's posts behind it, for as long as the relay. notifyAccount logs a failure itself and
 * never throws.
 */
export async function takeDownTerminated(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, facts: { decidedAt: Date; imagesSealed: boolean }): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  const revoked = await deps.repo.takeDownTerminated(user.id, deps.now());
  if (revoked === null) return false;
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, user.id, revoked);
  // 3f (7.15 step 8): a termination's take-down is held the same way, and its mail gains the same paragraph.
  const held = await heldAddressFacts(deps, user.id);
  void notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "termination_final", { decided: noticeTime(facts.decidedAt), imagesSealed: String(facts.imagesSealed), ...held });
  return true;
}

/**
 * Step 4 of section 7.6, which the purge job runs for every account left half deleted: the rows of
 * step 1 again (sessions still live revoked with their tombstones, devices, codes and passkeys deleted,
 * the WebAuthn user handle cleared), for an account marked deleted without the rest, then the row
 * anonymised and marked purged. Both parts change nothing for an account that is live or already
 * purged, so the job can repeat it after any failure. 3f (7.15): while REPORT_HOLD is on and the
 * account's address is held for a report, the credentials go and the address waits: the answer is then
 * `held`, and the account stays pending for the next round.
 */
export async function finishPurge(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<"purged" | "held" | "none"> {
  const revoked = await deps.repo.finishTakeDown(userId, deps.now());
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, userId, revoked);
  return deps.repo.finishPurge(userId, deps.now(), deps.config.reportHold);
}

import { RETENTION, type AlertFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { MailRefused, type MailMessage, type NoticeUpdateLine } from "../../mail/mailer";
import type { DecisionMailSubject } from "../../mail/templates";
import type { AuthDeps } from "../context";
import { decrypt, encrypt, randomToken, safeEqual } from "../crypto";
import { emailHash } from "../identifiers";
import { HOUR } from "../limits";
import { noticeTime } from "./notify";

/**
 * The auth module's side of reports and notices (3c design, section 5): a signed-out notifier's name and address, which
 * live here, encrypted, where the API's role cannot reach them, and every mail of the moderation module, which never
 * sees an address or a mail token. The moderation module names a contact by an id it chose, names an account by its id,
 * and passes typed messages: no caller passes free text, and this module builds every link itself.
 */

const DAY = 24 * HOUR;

/** An address that is not confirmed gets at most one receipt in this long; further ones are folded into the next daily mail. */
export const RECEIPT_CAP_MS = DAY;

/** The receipt of a report or a notice: its reference, when it was received, and the korbat links it named, in the order named. */
export interface NoticeReceivedMessage {
  template: "notice_received";
  ref: string;
  receivedAt: Date;
  items: readonly string[];
}

/** The daily update of decisions on the reports an account sent: its lines, as the moderation module composed them. */
export interface AccountUpdateMessage {
  template: "notice_update";
  lines: readonly NoticeUpdateLine[];
}

/**
 * The statement of reasons to the author of what a decision restricts or lifts: the subject by its key, and the
 * statement's paragraphs exactly as they were rendered for the author's screen. 3e (design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6):
 * a suspension or termination taken at once, and the lift of one (or its end when a reversal broke its basis), are
 * mailed under a subject and a lead of their own, with the same paragraphs; the moderation module picks the template
 * (mailTemplateOf). Times are instants, printed here as the notices print them.
 */
export type DecisionMessage =
  | { template: "moderation_decision"; subject: DecisionMailSubject; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: an announced measure, with its days (null for a termination), the reply window in hours and the earliest start.
  | { template: "suspension_announced"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; days: number | null; window: number; earliestStart: string; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "suspension_started_at_once"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; days: number | null; endsAt: string | null; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: the answer to the person's reply, which kept the measure in force or reversed it.
  | { template: "reply_answered"; outcome: "kept" | "reversed"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "suspension_lifted"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; why: "lifted" | "basis"; period: "not_started" | "running" | "ended"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: a withdrawal signed `replaced`, with the withdrawn decision's time and whether the person had replied to it.
  | { template: "suspension_lifted"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; why: "replaced"; decidedAt: string; replied: boolean; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 5: a warning about the account's reports; a restriction of them, with its days and its end.
  | { template: "reporting_warned"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "reporting_restricted"; days: number; endsAt: string; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3f Task 3 (design, W.5): an order's notice, a reinstatement after one, and the authority's words added to a notice
  // already told. Each says only that a notice is there or has grown: its paragraphs are not mailed, and are empty.
  | { template: "order_notice" | "order_reinstated_notice" | "order_notice_added"; paragraphs: readonly string[] };

/** The templates of a decision's statement mail: a stop of the address never holds one back. */
const DECISION_TEMPLATES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "moderation_decision",
  "suspension_announced",
  "suspension_started_at_once",
  "reply_answered",
  "suspension_lifted",
  "reporting_warned",
  "reporting_restricted",
  "order_notice",
  "order_reinstated_notice",
  "order_notice_added",
]);

/** Whether an account's message is a decision's statement. */
const isDecisionMessage = (message: { template: string }): message is DecisionMessage => DECISION_TEMPLATES.has(message.template);

/** What the statement's paragraphs are joined with in a mail's data: one paragraph per line. */
const LINE_BREAK = String.fromCharCode(10);

/** A decision's message as its template's flat data: one data value for the statement, one paragraph per line, exactly as it was rendered. */
function decisionData(message: DecisionMessage): Record<string, string> {
  const statement = message.paragraphs.join(LINE_BREAK);
  switch (message.template) {
    case "moderation_decision":
      return { subject: message.subject, statement };
    case "suspension_announced":
      return { measure: message.measure, statement, window: String(message.window), earliestStart: noticeTime(new Date(message.earliestStart)), ...(message.days === null ? {} : { days: String(message.days) }) };
    case "suspension_started_at_once":
      return { measure: message.measure, statement, ...(message.days === null ? {} : { days: String(message.days) }), ...(message.endsAt === null ? {} : { endsAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.endsAt)) }) };
    case "reply_answered":
      return { outcome: message.outcome, statement };
    case "suspension_lifted":
      return message.why === "replaced"
        ? { measure: message.measure, why: message.why, decidedAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.decidedAt)), replied: String(message.replied), statement }
        : { measure: message.measure, why: message.why, period: message.period, statement };
    case "reporting_warned":
      return { statement };
    case "reporting_restricted":
      return { statement, days: String(message.days), endsAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.endsAt)) };
    case "order_notice":
    case "order_reinstated_notice":
    case "order_notice_added":
      // A fixed body: nothing of the notice goes by mail.
      return {};
  }
}

/** What may be sent to a signed-out notifier's contact by itself: the receipt. Its updates go by address, through mailNotifierUpdates. */
export type NotifierMessage = NoticeReceivedMessage;
/** What may be sent to an account: the receipt and the daily update of its reports, and the statement of a decision about it. */
export type AccountMessage = NoticeReceivedMessage | AccountUpdateMessage | DecisionMessage;

/** One contact's share of the daily update: the lines of its notice, and its receipt when the 24-hour cap folded it. */
export interface NotifierUpdatePart {
  contactId: string;
  /** The reference of the contact's notice. */
  ref: string;
  lines: readonly NoticeUpdateLine[];
  receipt?: { ref: string; receivedAt: Date; items: readonly string[] };
}

/** What became of one contact's share: as a mail's result, or "unavailable" when the relay could not take that address's mail or the contact could not be read. */
export type NotifierUpdateResult = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "forgotten" | "refused" | "unavailable";

/**
 * The staff alerts: counts, times and a staff account's public handle, never a link or content. The urgent lane's alert;
 * the cases that wait longer than their lane's response time, and those that hold a measure taken while deciding for
 * more than a day; the staff account that confirmed many decisions in a short time; the one that reached its daily case
 * limit; every reveal of who sent a report, with the day's count; and every decision that lifted the protection of
 * images reported as child sexual abuse material.
 */
export type StaffMessage =
  | StaffAlertMessage
  | { template: "moderation_urgent"; count: number; oldest: Date }
  | { template: "moderation_waiting"; lanes: readonly { lane: 0 | 1 | 2; count: number; oldest: Date }[]; interim: number; replies?: { count: number; oldest: Date } | null }
  | { template: "moderation_burst"; handle: string; count: number }
  | { template: "moderation_reads"; handle: string; limit: number }
  | { template: "moderation_reveal"; handle: string; at: Date; count: number; limit: number }
  | { template: "moderation_csam_lifted"; handle: string; at: Date; what: "unsealed" | "dismissed" };

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 7.2, 7.19 and 18, W.4): the staff alerts whose mail is their push's sentence, which the alert tick
 * mails from a row of alert_outbox: the row's facts, counts and times only, and nothing else. Later tasks of 3f add their
 * kinds here as they first write them.
 */
export type StaffAlertKind =
  | "contact_mail"
  | "contact_mail_escalated"
  | "order_due"
  | "mailbox_unreachable"
  | "alert_channel_down"
  | "order_opened"
  | "order_corrected"
  | "order_unverified"
  // Task 3: an order given effect, an order's measure lifted, and a held notice about to be released.
  | "order_effected"
  | "order_reinstated"
  | "hold_ending"
  // Task 6: the copy of the audit log's tail is overdue, and someone who did not take the last copy took one.
  | "copy_overdue"
  | "copy_taken"
  // Task 5's two daily kinds, joined in 3f's review: a report to an authority owed, a hand-over's copy not destroyed.
  | "report_owed"
  | "handover_undestroyed";
export interface StaffAlertMessage {
  template: StaffAlertKind;
  facts: AlertFacts;
}

/**
 * A staff alert's template data: every member as the text the template prints. A 3f alert's facts go as they are, each
 * count as its digits, with the time it is sent: the template prints a time with its day only when that is not today's.
 */
function staffData(message: StaffMessage, now: Date): Record<string, string> {
  switch (message.template) {
    case "contact_mail":
    case "contact_mail_escalated":
    case "order_due":
    case "mailbox_unreachable":
    case "alert_channel_down":
    case "order_opened":
    case "order_corrected":
    case "order_unverified":
    case "order_effected":
    case "order_reinstated":
    case "hold_ending":
    case "copy_overdue":
    case "copy_taken":
    case "report_owed":
    case "handover_undestroyed":
      return { ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(message.facts).map(([name, value]) => [name, String(value)])), now: now.toISOString() };
    case "moderation_urgent":
      return { count: String(message.count), oldest: noticeTime(message.oldest) };
    case "moderation_waiting": {
      // A lane's pair only for a lane with a case past its time, and the measures' count only when it is not 0.
      const data: Record<string, string> = {};
      for (const lane of message.lanes) {
        if (lane.count <= 0) continue;
        data[`lane${lane.lane}Count`] = String(lane.count);
        data[`lane${lane.lane}Oldest`] = noticeTime(lane.oldest);
      }
      if (message.interim > 0) data.interimCount = String(message.interim);
      // 3e Task 4: the replies unanswered for longer than korbat's aim, only when there are any.
      if (message.replies && message.replies.count > 0) {
        data.replyCount = String(message.replies.count);
        data.replyOldest = noticeTime(message.replies.oldest);
      }
      return data;
    }
    case "moderation_burst":
      return { handle: message.handle, count: String(message.count) };
    case "moderation_csam_lifted":
      return { handle: message.handle, time: noticeTime(message.at), what: message.what };
    case "moderation_reads":
      return { handle: message.handle, limit: String(message.limit) };
    case "moderation_reveal":
      return { handle: message.handle, time: noticeTime(message.at), count: String(message.count), limit: String(message.limit) };
  }
}

export type NotifierMailResult = "sent" | "folded" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "forgotten" | "refused";
export type AccountMailResult = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "refused";

/** What staff may know of a signed-out notifier without a reveal: never the name or the address themselves. */
export interface NotifierFacts {
  /** False for an id no contact has: it was never stored, or the janitor has forgotten it. Then the other four are false too. */
  found: boolean;
  named: boolean;
  contactGiven: boolean;
  confirmed: boolean;
  suppressed: boolean;
}

/** A contact's ciphertexts open under the key, or under a key it replaced. Nothing read is ever written back under the newer key. */
const open = (deps: Pick<AuthDeps, "config">, payload: string): string => decrypt(payload, [deps.config.notifierKey, ...deps.config.notifierPreviousKeys]).toString("utf8");
const seal = (deps: AuthDeps, plain: string): string => encrypt(Buffer.from(plain, "utf8"), deps.config.notifierKey);

/** The same day `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsLater(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** The cap's marker for an address, by its keyed hash: set when a receipt goes to it unconfirmed, gone a day later. */
const receiptCapKey = (hash: string) => `notifier-receipt:${hash}`;

/** The receipt's template data. The page link is this module's: the status page's address with the contact's mail token in the fragment, which no server log sees. */
function receiptData(deps: AuthDeps, message: NoticeReceivedMessage, pageUrl?: string): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    ref: message.ref,
    time: noticeTime(message.receivedAt),
    items: message.items.join(", "),
    ...(pageUrl === undefined ? {} : { pageUrl }),
    termsUrl: `${deps.config.appOrigin}/terms`,
  };
}

/** Sends one mail. "refused" when the relay refused the recipient for good; any other failure is thrown, for the caller to try again. */
async function deliver(deps: AuthDeps, message: MailMessage): Promise<"sent" | "refused"> {
  try {
    await deps.mailer.send(message);
    return "sent";
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof MailRefused) return "refused";
    throw err;
  }
}

/**
 * Stores a signed-out notifier's contact under the id the moderation module wrote on the notice: the name and the
 * address normalised and encrypted under the notifier key, the address's keyed hash for the cap and for stops, and, with
 * an address, a fresh mail token encrypted beside it. A disposable address is taken: a notifier may want one. The contact
 * is forgotten 13 months on unless the notice is still owed something by then.
 */
export async function storeNotifierContact(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, contact: { name?: string; email?: string }): Promise<void> {
  const name = contact.name?.trim() || null;
  const email = contact.email?.trim().toLowerCase() || null;
  await deps.repo.createNotifierContact({
    id: contactId,
    nameEnc: name === null ? null : seal(deps, name),
    emailEnc: email === null ? null : seal(deps, email),
    emailHash: email === null ? null : emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, email),
    // The token of the mails' link: it alone confirms or stops the address, so whoever typed someone else's address cannot.
    mailTokenEnc: email === null ? null : seal(deps, randomToken()),
    forgetAfter: monthsLater(deps.now(), RETENTION.contactMaxMonths),
  });
}

/**
 * Sends a signed-out notifier's receipt, under three rules. A stopped address gets nothing ("suppressed"). An address
 * that is not confirmed gets one receipt in 24 hours, and a further one is "folded": it rides in the next daily mail, so
 * typing someone's address into the form many times sends them one mail. A confirmed address has no cap. "forgotten"
 * when no contact has the id, "no_address" when the contact left none. A failure of the relay that is not about the
 * address is thrown, and gives the day's one receipt back first, so the retry is sent rather than folded.
 */
export async function mailNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, message: NotifierMessage): Promise<NotifierMailResult> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  if (!contact) return "forgotten";
  if (!contact.emailEnc || !contact.emailHash || !contact.mailTokenEnc) return "no_address";
  const hash = contact.emailHash;
  if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash)) return "suppressed";
  // Opened before the cap is taken: a ciphertext no configured key opens throws here and spends nothing.
  const to = open(deps, contact.emailEnc);
  const pageUrl = `${deps.config.appOrigin}/notice/${message.ref}#t=${open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc)}`;
  const confirmed = (await deps.repo.confirmedNotifierHashes([hash], deps.now())).has(hash);
  if (!confirmed && !(await deps.kv.setIfAbsent(receiptCapKey(hash), "1", RECEIPT_CAP_MS))) return "folded";
  try {
    return await deliver(deps, { to, template: "notice_received", data: receiptData(deps, message, pageUrl) });
  } catch (err) {
    if (!confirmed) await deps.kv.del(receiptCapKey(hash)).catch((failure: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err: failure }, "notifier receipt: the day's one receipt could not be given back after a failed send"));
    throw err;
  }
}

/**
 * Sends a mail to an account's own address, which its sign-in code confirmed: no cap and no confirmation. A stop of
 * that address applies to the two report mails, the receipt and the daily update, and never to a statement of reasons.
 * The update of an account is signed in: it carries its lines and neither a receipt nor a page link, since an account
 * follows its reports in the app. "no_address" for an account that is deleted or was never there.
 */
export async function mailAccount(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, message: AccountMessage): Promise<AccountMailResult> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return "no_address";
  if (isDecisionMessage(message)) {
    // A statement is never held back by a stop of the address.
    return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: message.template, data: decisionData(message) });
  }
  const hash = emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email);
  if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash)) return "suppressed";
  if (message.template === "notice_update") return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: "notice_update", data: { signedIn: true, lines: [...message.lines], receipts: [], pages: [] } });
  return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: "notice_received", data: receiptData(deps, message) });
}

/**
 * The daily update to signed-out notifiers (3c design, sections 5 and 7.8): the parts are grouped by their contacts'
 * address, which only this module can see, and each address gets one notice_update with every part's lines, every
 * carried receipt with its page link, and the page link of each other notice it has a line for. A page link is the
 * status page's address with that contact's own mail token in the fragment, the same link its receipt carried.
 *
 * It applies a stop of the address, and neither the confirmation nor the 24-hour cap: nothing is withheld for want of a
 * confirmed address. It answers for each contact, and throws for none: an address whose mail the relay could not take is
 * "unavailable", so its lines stay pending while every other address's update is still sent. Each contact is read in a
 * try of its own: one that cannot be read (a ciphertext no configured key opens) is logged with its id, never an
 * address, and answered "unavailable" too.
 */
export async function mailNotifierUpdates(deps: AuthDeps, parts: readonly NotifierUpdatePart[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>> {
  const results = new Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>();
  /** The readable parts, by their address's keyed hash, in the order given. */
  const byAddress = new Map<string, { to: string; parts: { part: NotifierUpdatePart; pageUrl: string }[] }>();
  for (const part of parts) {
    try {
      const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(part.contactId);
      if (!contact) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "forgotten");
        continue;
      }
      if (!contact.emailEnc || !contact.emailHash || !contact.mailTokenEnc) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "no_address");
        continue;
      }
      if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([contact.emailHash])).has(contact.emailHash)) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "suppressed");
        continue;
      }
      const to = open(deps, contact.emailEnc);
      const pageUrl = `${deps.config.appOrigin}/notice/${part.ref}#t=${open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc)}`;
      const group = byAddress.get(contact.emailHash) ?? { to, parts: [] };
      group.parts.push({ part, pageUrl });
      byAddress.set(contact.emailHash, group);
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, contactId: part.contactId }, "notifier update: the contact could not be read; its lines stay pending");
      results.set(part.contactId, "unavailable");
    }
  }
  for (const group of byAddress.values()) {
    const receipts = group.parts.flatMap(({ part, pageUrl }) => (part.receipt ? [{ ref: part.receipt.ref, time: noticeTime(part.receipt.receivedAt), items: part.receipt.items.join(", "), pageUrl }] : []));
    // A notice whose receipt rides in this update has its page with the receipt; every other notice with a line gets a page paragraph.
    const pages = group.parts.flatMap(({ part, pageUrl }) => (part.receipt || part.lines.length === 0 ? [] : [{ ref: part.ref, pageUrl }]));
    const lines = group.parts.flatMap(({ part }) => [...part.lines]);
    let result: NotifierUpdateResult;
    try {
      result = await deliver(deps, {
        to: group.to,
        template: "notice_update",
        data: { signedIn: false, lines, receipts, pages, ...(receipts.length > 0 ? { termsUrl: `${deps.config.appOrigin}/terms` } : {}) },
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // The relay could not take this address's mail: the other addresses' mails still go. The contacts' ids, never the address.
      deps.log.warn({ err, contactIds: group.parts.map(({ part }) => part.contactId) }, "notifier update: not sent; its lines stay pending for the next round");
      result = "unavailable";
    }
    for (const { part } of group.parts) results.set(part.contactId, result);
  }
  // In the order the parts were given, whatever order the addresses were mailed in.
  return new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.contactId, results.get(part.contactId) ?? "unavailable"]));
}

/**
 * Sends a staff alert to every live staff account's address, best effort: a failed send is logged and never thrown, and
 * the answer is the number of addresses the relay took, 0 when it took none or there is no live staff account. It
 * applies no throttle: the moderation module keeps every throttle, as a key in the shared limit store.
 */
export async function mailStaff(deps: AuthDeps, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number> {
  const data = staffData(message, deps.now());
  let addresses: string[];
  try {
    addresses = await deps.repo.liveStaffAddresses();
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, template: message.template }, "staff alert: the staff accounts could not be read");
    return 0;
  }
  let accepted = 0;
  for (const to of addresses) {
    try {
      await deps.mailer.send({ to, template: message.template, data });
      accepted++;
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, template: message.template }, "staff alert email failed");
    }
  }
  return accepted;
}

/** For each id: whether a contact has it, whether a name and an address were given, and whether the address is confirmed or stopped now. */
export async function notifierFacts(deps: AuthDeps, contactIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierFacts>> {
  const rows = await deps.repo.notifierContactFacts(contactIds);
  const hashes = rows.flatMap((row) => (row.emailHash === null ? [] : [row.emailHash]));
  const [confirmed, suppressed] = await Promise.all([deps.repo.confirmedNotifierHashes(hashes, deps.now()), deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes(hashes)]);
  const byId = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
  return new Map(
    contactIds.map((id): [string, NotifierFacts] => {
      const row = byId.get(id);
      if (!row) return [id, { found: false, named: false, contactGiven: false, confirmed: false, suppressed: false }];
      return [id, { found: true, named: row.named, contactGiven: row.contactGiven, confirmed: row.emailHash !== null && confirmed.has(row.emailHash), suppressed: row.emailHash !== null && suppressed.has(row.emailHash) }];
    }),
  );
}

/** The name a notifier gave, or null: for a confirmed reveal only. The address is never handed out. */
export async function notifierName(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  return contact?.nameEnc ? open(deps, contact.nameEnc) : null;
}

/** The contact's address hash when the token is its mail token, compared in constant time; null for anything else. */
async function addressOfToken(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  if (!contact?.mailTokenEnc || !contact.emailHash) return null;
  let mailToken: string;
  try {
    mailToken = open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc);
  } catch (err) {
    // A contact no configured key opens matches nothing; the fault is the operator's to see, with the contact's id and no address.
    deps.log.error({ err, contactId }, "notifier contact: its mail token could not be decrypted");
    return null;
  }
  return safeEqual(mailToken, token) ? contact.emailHash : null;
}

/** Whether the token is the contact's mail token; false when the contact has none. */
export async function notifierMailTokenMatches(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token)) !== null;
}

/**
 * "I sent this": with the contact's mail token, records the address as confirmed for 30 days and lifts any stop of it.
 * False, and nothing done, for any other token: typing someone's address proves nothing about it.
 */
export async function confirmNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const hash = await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token);
  if (hash === null) return false;
  const now = deps.now();
  await deps.repo.confirmNotifierAddress(hash, now, new Date(now.getTime() + RETENTION.confirmationDays * DAY));
  return true;
}

/** "Stop": with the contact's mail token, korbat sends this address no more mails about reports. Its notices are still processed. */
export async function stopNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const hash = await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token);
  if (hash === null) return false;
  await deps.repo.suppressNotifierAddress(hash);
  return true;
}

/** Whether the account's address asked korbat to stop its report mails. */
export async function accountReportMailStopped(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  const hash = emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email);
  return (await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash);
}

/** Lifts a stop of the account's address, for the account's own Settings: the session proves the address. True when there was one. */
export async function resumeAccountReportMail(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  return deps.repo.liftNotifierSuppression(emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email));
}

/** Moves the day these contacts are forgotten. */
export function forgetNotifierAfter(deps: AuthDeps, contactIds: readonly string[], at: Date): Promise<void> {
  return deps.repo.setNotifierForgetAfter(contactIds, at);
}

/** The contacts that gave this address, with the names they gave: for an access request from a signed-out notifier, from the command line only. */
export async function findNotifierContacts(deps: Pick<AuthDeps, "repo" | "config">, email: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string | null }[]> {
  const rows = await deps.repo.notifierContactsByEmailHash(emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, email));
  return rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, name: row.nameEnc ? open(deps, row.nameEnc) : null }));
}

/** How many contacts and confirmations the janitor should have removed more than a day ago: a count only, for the console's overview. */
export function overdueContacts(deps: AuthDeps): Promise<number> {
  return deps.repo.countNotifierRowsDue(new Date(deps.now().getTime() - DAY));
}

} from "@korbat/db";

/**
 * Every SQL statement the auth module runs. It receives only the korbat_auth pool and touches only
 * tables in the `auth` schema. Single-use and replay rules are enforced with conditional updates so
 * two concurrent requests cannot both succeed.
 */

export type UserRow = typeof users.$inferSelect;
export type DeviceRow = typeof devices.$inferSelect;

export type EmailCodePurpose = (typeof emailCodePurpose.enumValues)[number];

/** What a registration stores of a verified passkey; the id, the last use and the suspicion are the row's own. */
export type NewPasskey = Omit<PasskeyRow, "id" | "lastUsedAt" | "suspectAt">;

export interface PasskeyLimits {

}

/** What addPasskey answers: the row it inserted; which bound refused it, with the seconds until the day has a slot again; or that the account is gone. */

export interface LockDownInput {

  enrollmentsDeleted: number;
  /** The staff keys revoked by a change to user, oldest first. */
  keysRevoked: { id: string; name: string }[];
}

export interface SessionListRow {
  /** The hash of the session's token, which its cached copy is keyed by; it changes when the token rotates and is never shown to a client. */
  id: string;
  /** The session's id for life: what the list shows, and what the targeted revoke takes. */
  handle: string;
  deviceLabel: string | null;
  platform: string;
  createdAt: Date;
  lastUsedAt: Date;
}

export function createAuthRepo(db: Db) {
  return {
    // ------------------------------------------------------------ users

    async findUserByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(users)
        .where(and(sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${email})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    async findUserById(id: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(users)
        .where(and(eq(users.id, id), isNull(users.deletedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** The email is already verified (the user proved it with a code) and the age check has passed. */
    async createUser(input: { email: string; termsVersion: string; now: Date }): Promise<UserRow> {
      const [row] = await db
        .insert(users)
        .values({
          email: input.email,
          emailVerifiedAt: input.now,
          ageConfirmedAt: input.now,
          termsVersion: input.termsVersion,
          termsAcceptedAt: input.now,
        })
        .returning();
      return row!;
    },

    async markOnboarded(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ onboardedAt: now }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * Moves the account to an address its owner just proved with a code, so it is verified as of now.
     * When another row holds the address, in any case, the unique index on lower(email) raises the
     * driver's unique violation; the flow reports that as email_in_use.
     */
    async changeEmail(userId: string, email: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ email, emailVerifiedAt: now }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * The keyed hash of the phone number behind the verified badge, or null to drop it. When another row
     * holds the same hash, the partial unique index on phone_hash raises the driver's unique violation;
     * the flow reports that as phone_in_use.
     */
    async setPhoneHash(userId: string, phoneHash: string | null): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ phoneHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Setting or clearing a password also clears any password lockout. */
    async setPasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string | null, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ passwordHash, passwordChangedAt: now, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Replaces the hash only, after a sign-in verified the password against older parameters. */
    async replacePasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ passwordHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async setPasswordFailures(userId: string, failedLogins: number, lockedUntil: Date | null): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ failedLogins, lockedUntil }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async enableTotp(userId: string, input: { secretEnc: string; recoveryCodesHash: string[]; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpSecretEnc: input.secretEnc, totpEnabledAt: input.now, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: input.recoveryCodesHash })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async disableTotp(userId: string): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** The same secret re-encrypted with the current key; nothing else about MFA changes. */
    async setTotpSecretEnc(userId: string, totpSecretEnc: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ totpSecretEnc }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async setRecoveryCodes(userId: string, recoveryCodesHash: string[]): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ recoveryCodesHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Claims a TOTP time step. False when this step or a later one was already used. */
    async claimTotpStep(userId: string, step: number): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpLastStep: step })
        .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), or(isNull(users.totpLastStep), lt(users.totpLastStep, step))))
        .returning({ id: users.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Removes one recovery-code hash. False when it is not (or no longer) present. */
    async consumeRecoveryCodeHash(userId: string, codeHash: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ recoveryCodesHash: sql`array_remove(${users.recoveryCodesHash}, ${codeHash})` })
        .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), sql`${codeHash} = ANY(${users.recoveryCodesHash})`))
        .returning({ id: users.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    async setRole(userId: string, role: UserRole): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ role }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * A role change (3a design, section 7) in one transaction: the account's row is locked first, FOR NO KEY UPDATE (the
     * lock the role's update would take, and the one every writer of staff rows takes first, so none of them can wait on
     * another in a circle); the role is set, every session and every staff session revoked and every unused enrolment link
     * deleted, so the new role applies at once and no link issued before enrols anything. A change to user also revokes
     * every staff key, with a staff_key_revoked event each: a person made staff again enrols new keys. Last, through
     * auth.append_audit, each revocation's audit row and then the role_granted row, which hold the audit chain's head until
     * the commit, so the change and its record commit together or not at all. Only the command line calls this, and it
     * waits at most 10 seconds for a lock: an API that holds the head or the row open cannot stall it for longer, and one
     * that times out has changed nothing. The cache tombstones and the mail are not the database's to write, so the caller
     * does them after the commit with what this answers; undefined when no live account has the address.
     *
     * 3e (design, section 7.16): no suspended account becomes staff. For a promotion, auth.account_standing is asked in a
     * statement of its own after the row's lock: a deciding transaction reads the same row FOR SHARE, so it either waited
     * for this one and then meets staff_target, or committed first and is read here. When the account holds a standing
     * suspension, termination or restriction of reporting nothing is changed and the answer is "standing".
     */
    async changeRole(email: string, role: UserRole, audit: { actorId: string; now: Date }): Promise<RoleChange | "standing" | undefined> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        const [account] = await tx
          .select({ id: users.id, email: users.email, role: users.role })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${email})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
          .limit(1)
          .for("no key update");
        if (!account) return undefined;
        if (role !== "user") {
          const [standing] = await tx.execute<{ held: boolean }>(sql`select auth.account_standing(${account.id}::uuid) as held`);
          // Nothing was written: the transaction ends with the row's lock and no audit row.
          if (standing!.held) return "standing";
        }
        await tx.update(users).set({ role }).where(eq(users.id, account.id));
        const revoked = await tx
          .update(sessions)
          .set({ revokedAt: audit.now })
          .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, account.id), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ id: sessions.id });
        const staff = await revokeStaffAccess(tx, account.id, audit.now, { keys: role === "user", enrollments: "unused", via: "role_change" });
        await appendKeyRevocations(tx, audit.actorId, staff, "role_change");
        await appendAudit(tx, {
          actorId: audit.actorId,
          action: "role_granted",
          targetType: "user",
          targetId: account.id,
          // A role change deletes open links only, so every link it deleted was one it cancelled.
          metadata: { from: account.role, to: role, via: "cli", staffSessionsRevoked: staff.staffSessionsRevoked, enrollmentsDeleted: staff.enrollmentsCancelled },
        });
        return {
          userId: account.id,
          email: account.email,
          previousRole: account.role,
          sessionIds: revoked.map((row) => row.id),
          staffSessionsRevoked: staff.staffSessionsRevoked,
          enrollmentsDeleted: staff.enrollmentsCancelled,
          keysRevoked: staff.keys.map(({ id, name }) => ({ id, name })),
        };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ deletion

    /**
     * Marks the row deleted and nothing else: from now on every lookup above treats it as absent. Once only; a
     * later call changes nothing. A deletion goes through takeDown; this is the state a take-down that stopped
     * after the mark would leave, which finishTakeDown completes.
     */
    async markDeleted(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)));
    },

    /**
     * Step 1 of a deletion (1b design, section 7.6) in one transaction: the row is marked deleted, every live
     * session revoked, every device, code and passkey deleted, the WebAuthn user handle cleared, the account's staff
     * keys and staff sessions revoked, its enrolment links deleted and its keys blanked (3a design, section 7), and the
     * account_deleted event appended; last, the audit rows of the staff side, with the account as their actor, since its
     * owner asked for the deletion. Either all of it lands or none of it does, so a failure leaves a live account with its
     * sessions, never a deleted one with sessions, devices, passkeys or staff keys that nothing would remove. Answers the
     * ids of the sessions it revoked, for the cache tombstones, which are not the database's to write.
     */
    async takeDown(userId: string, now: Date, deviceId: string | null): Promise<string[]> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)));
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId, metadata: {} });
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, userId, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /**
     * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.8): the take-down of a terminated account, as the system and not its owner. In one
     * transaction, as takeDown: the row marked deleted, step 1's rows, the account_deleted event (its metadata says that a
     * final termination took it down), and last the staff side's audit rows with the server as their actor. Only for a row
     * that this call marks: one already marked deleted (a round whose purge failed after the take-down, or the owner's own
     * deletion) is left as it is, nothing is written and the answer is null. Else the ids of the sessions it revoked.
     */
    async takeDownTerminated(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string[] | null> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const marked = await tx.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt))).returning({ id: users.id });
        if (marked.length === 0) return null;
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId: null, metadata: { terminated: true } });
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /**
     * The rows of step 1 again (the sessions, devices, codes and passkeys, the WebAuthn user handle and the staff rows), for
     * a row marked deleted and not purged yet: a take-down that stopped after the mark, or a session that a sign-in already
     * past its lookup created after it. Nothing for a live or a purged row. The account_deleted event is not appended
     * again: the confirmation that recorded it is the only one there was. The staff side's audit rows are written, last,
     * for what this run revoked, with the server as their actor: the purge job finishes the take-down, no person.
     */
    async finishTakeDown(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        // The account's row first, as every writer of staff rows takes it (3a design, section 7).
        const [row] = await tx
          .select({ id: users.id })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)))
          .for("no key update");
        if (!row) return [];
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /**
     * Deleted accounts whose row the purge has not anonymised yet, oldest deletion first, at most 100 a round. 3f (design,
     * section 7.15 step 5): an account whose address is held for a report to the authorities stays pending until its hold
     * ends, and comes last, so that held rows never crowd out the round's 100.
     */
    async pendingPurges(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: users.id })
        .from(users)
        .where(and(isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)))
        .orderBy(sql`auth.address_held(${users.id})`, users.deletedAt, users.id)
        .limit(100);
      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
    },

    /**
     * The last step of a deletion: every credential and personal fact is cleared, the address becomes deleted:<id>
     * (unique, and never a real address), and purged_at says it is done. Only a deleted row not purged yet is written, so
     * a second call, or a call for a live account, changes nothing.
     *
     * 3f (design, sections 6.5 and 7.15): two statements, in one transaction. The first clears the credentials and the
     * personal facts but the address, without condition: the password hash, the TOTP secret, the recovery codes, the phone
     * hash, the age and terms marks. The second overwrites the address and sets purged_at only where
     * auth.address_held(id) is false, while `holdAddress` (REPORT_HOLD) is on: a report of the account's sealed images is
     * owed, and the law may oblige korbat to give the address with it. One update with that condition on all of it would
     * keep the credentials too; the hold is for the address alone. Answers what it did: purged, held (the address waits,
     * and the next round tries again), or none (nothing to do).
     */
    async finishPurge(userId: string, now: Date, holdAddress = true): Promise<"purged" | "held" | "none"> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const cleared = await tx
          .update(users)
          .set({
            passwordHash: null,
            totpSecretEnc: null,
            totpEnabledAt: null,
            recoveryCodesHash: [],
            phoneHash: null,
            ageConfirmedAt: null,
            termsVersion: null,
            termsAcceptedAt: null,
          })
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)))
          .returning({ id: users.id });
        if (cleared.length === 0) return "none";
        const purged = await tx
          .update(users)
          .set({ email: `deleted:${userId}`, emailVerifiedAt: null, purgedAt: now })
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt), holdAddress ? sql`not auth.address_held(${users.id})` : undefined))
          .returning({ id: users.id });
        return purged.length > 0 ? "purged" : "held";
      });
    },

    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.15 step 2): what the deletion mail says of a held address: until when at the latest (a UTC
     * day) and whether the seal behind it is for good, or null when nothing is held. The auth module cannot read the hold
     * itself; it asks the two definer functions the migration grants it. 3f's review (access3): and whether the person
     * was told of the seals behind it (auth.address_hold_told): false while one is held with an order's notice, and the
     * mail then says nothing of the hold.
     */
    async addressHold(userId: string): Promise<{ until: Date; final: boolean; told: boolean } | null> {
      const [row] = await db.execute<{ until: string | null; final: boolean; told: boolean }>(
        sql`select to_char(auth.address_held_until(${userId}::uuid) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as until, auth.address_hold_final(${userId}::uuid) as final,
                   auth.address_hold_told(${userId}::uuid) as told`,
      );
      return row?.until ? { until: new Date(row.until), final: row.final, told: row.told } : null;
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ lockdown

    /**
     * The lockdown (1c design, sections 2 and 7.6) in one transaction, as takeDown is one: every live session
     * revoked, every device revoked (so the next sign-in on any of them counts as a new device), the password
     * cleared as setPasswordHash clears it, the passkeys in reach removed, two-factor turned off as disableTotp
     * does when it was enabled at or after `since`, and the caller's event appended with what was done. Either
     * all of it lands or none of it does: the link that started it is spent by then, so a lockdown that stopped
     * halfway could not be asked for again, and would be on no record. The user row is locked first, as takeDown
     * and a registration take it first, so none of the three can wait on another in a circle, and two-factor is
     * read from the locked row. Answers the ids of the sessions it revoked, for the cache tombstones, which are
     * not the database's to write.
     */
    async lockDown(userId: string, input: LockDownInput): Promise<LockDownOutcome> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        // An account that is gone has no two-factor to clear; its rows, if any are left, are still locked down below.
        const [locked] = await tx
          .select({ totpEnabledAt: users.totpEnabledAt })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)))
          .for("update");
        const revoked = await tx
          .update(sessions)
          .set({ revokedAt: input.now })
          .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, userId), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ id: sessions.id });
        await tx.update(devices).set({ revokedAt: input.now }).where(and(eq(devices.userId, userId), isNull(devices.revokedAt)));
        // The user's passkeys from `since` on, plus any of theirs the caller names; a named passkey of another account is not the caller's to remove and stays.
        const reach = input.passkeyIds.length > 0 ? or(gte(passkeys.createdAt, input.since), inArray(passkeys.id, [...input.passkeyIds])) : gte(passkeys.createdAt, input.since);
        const removed = await tx
          .delete(passkeys)
          .where(and(eq(passkeys.userId, userId), reach))
          .returning({ id: passkeys.id });
        const totpCleared = locked !== undefined && locked.totpEnabledAt !== null && locked.totpEnabledAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime();
        await tx
          .update(users)
          .set({
            passwordHash: null,
            passwordChangedAt: input.now,
            failedLogins: 0,
            lockedUntil: null,
            ...(totpCleared ? { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] } : {}),
          })
          .where(eq(users.id, userId));
        const passkeysRemoved = removed.map((row) => row.id);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({
          userId,
          type: input.event.type,
          deviceId: input.event.deviceId,
          ipHash: input.event.ipHash,
          metadata: { ...input.event.metadata, passkeysRemoved, totpCleared, passwordCleared: true },
        });
        return { sessionIds: revoked.map((row) => row.id), passkeysRemoved, totpCleared };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ email codes

    async createEmailCode(input: {
      flowId: string;
      email: string;
      userId: string | null;
      purpose: EmailCodePurpose;
      codeHash: string;
      expiresAt: Date;
      ipHash: string | null;
    }): Promise<void> {
      await db.insert(emailCodes).values(input);
    },

    async findEmailCode(flowId: string): Promise<EmailCodeRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db.select().from(emailCodes).where(eq(emailCodes.flowId, flowId)).limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** Increments the attempt counter atomically and returns the new value. */
    async addCodeAttempt(id: string): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = await db
        .update(emailCodes)
        .set({ attempts: sql`${emailCodes.attempts} + 1` })
        .where(eq(emailCodes.id, id))
        .returning({ attempts: emailCodes.attempts });
      return row?.attempts ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
    },

    /** Marks a code used. False when it was already used, so a code works exactly once. */
    async consumeEmailCode(id: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(emailCodes)
        .set({ consumedAt: now })
        .where(and(eq(emailCodes.id, id), isNull(emailCodes.consumedAt)))
        .returning({ id: emailCodes.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ devices

    async findDevice(userId: string, deviceHash: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(devices)
        .where(and(eq(devices.userId, userId), eq(devices.deviceHash, deviceHash), isNull(devices.revokedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** The device by its row id, revoked or not: a session's device, whose platform names a passkey and whose label the passkey notices carry. */
    async findDeviceById(id: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db.select().from(devices).where(eq(devices.id, id)).limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    async createDevice(input: { userId: string; deviceHash: string; label: string; platform: string; ipHash: string | null }): Promise<DeviceRow> {
      const [row] = await db.insert(devices).values(input).returning();
      return row!;
    },

    async touchDevice(id: string, ipHash: string | null, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(devices).set({ lastSeenAt: now, ipHash }).where(eq(devices.id, id));
    },

    /** A revoked device no longer carries live sessions and counts as new at its next sign-in. */
    async revokeDevice(id: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(devices).set({ revokedAt: now }).where(and(eq(devices.id, id), isNull(devices.revokedAt)));
    },

    /** The user's devices that are not revoked, oldest first, for the data export; a revoked one stands for nothing of the account's any more. */
    async listDevices(userId: string): Promise<{ label: string | null; platform: string; firstSeenAt: Date; lastSeenAt: Date }[]> {
      return db
        .select({ label: devices.label, platform: devices.platform, firstSeenAt: devices.firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt: devices.lastSeenAt })
        .from(devices)
